A great merchant in %s2_city believes his contributions are unappreciated and he threatens to leave your service unless he receives considerable remuneration.
Thank him for his service and allow him to pursue his own interests.
We cannot allow him to fall into the service of our enemies, have him killed.

A stone has fallen from the sky and landed outside the city of %s2_city. It continues to burn even days after its descent. Our scholars claim that it is a fragment of Bhall's heaven. What should we do with the stone?
Sell the stone to fill our treasury.
Have one of our enchanters imbue a staff with the stone's power.
It is a religious artifact, keep it to remind us of Bhall's power.
Scouts report strange creatures moving within the smoke.
A wealthy woman in %s2_city was found dead in her study, the back of her head crushed in by a hammer. The judge asks for your wisdom in the matter.
Convict the husband. He claims he heard her scream and ran into the study to find her body.

Convict the butler. Some say he was having an affair with the woman, and he claims to have been sleeping in his room across from the study when the murder happened. He was awoken by the husband's screams for help.

Convict the houseguard. He had only been working in the house for a few weeks and is new to the city. He was guarding the front door to the manor and ran up to the study after hearing the husband's screams.
There isn't enough evidence to convict, let all three go.
Your people have discovered rare edible mushrooms.
Your unit encounters a flare of chaos mana.
Enter the flare, it will strengthen our unit.
Don't go near it, it is too dangerous.

Our people have found a tree in the forests outside of %s2_city that sparkles with thousands of lights after sunset. People are awed by the beauty of it, though some say the spirits of the dead dance in its branches.
Such a spectacle shouldn't be hidden in the forest. Cut it down and have it moved to the city's courtyard.
Hire some priests to calm those spirits and send them into the afterlife.
This is a gift of Cernunnos, make the area around the tree a sacred grove.
This defies the natural order, a tree should only be alight while burning. See that the natural order is restored...
A riot has broken out between Order and Veil worshipers in %s2_city.
Order the local militia to arrest the Veil rioters.

An orphanage in %s2_city has burnt down. The restless souls of the children killed in the fire continue to haunt the area.
There is little we can do.
Sanctify the area to put their souls to rest.
Bind their souls into our service.

Request that some of the Radiant Guard be stationed in your empire
Allow the councilors to train your priests

Your %s3_unit comes to you. Parith, an elven diplomat from the Umbrawood, has brought news that the elves are under attack. Your unit wants permission to leave this region and travel to the Umbrawood to aide the elves.
No, we cannot afford to have you march off to a distant war that is probably long over.
Penguins have settled on a cold coastal part of your empire. Their antics entertain your people.

An enormous giant arrives at the outskirts of %s2_city. He looks over the local herd with a greedy leer and licks his pointed teeth; some pigs appear to recognize him and begin a pitiful squealing.[NEWLINE]"Ikol's pigs run away," he says. "Neighbors give back."
These worthless pigs are thin and sick. But our larders are heavy, friend, join us in a feast to remember!
Get your own, you slobbering oaf.

The queen of the Calabim invites you to experience the richness of her capital. Your advisors warn that men who do not live up to Alexis's expectations are killed or doomed to spend the rest of their life in the Calabim breeding pits. Some say that even those that perform well end up in the pits.

Now you know why men still chase the dangerous Alexis, she is so beautiful that the hearts she is said to drink from could be given to her willingly. Despite the rumors you are allowed to leave the Calabim lands without difficulty, albeit with a few bite and scratch marks.
The summer court makes camp at the borders of the Ljosalfar empire. Arendel invites you to share a night of song and drink.
Visions of Arendel and the memory of her touch will haunt you. You flee to your ship before her beauty makes you incapable of enjoying anyone else.
A Bannor runner arrives at your capital with the message that Capria invites you to her palace for a private conference.
The Bannor's focus on discipline and strength applies even to their queen's bedchambers. You leave feeling refreshed, but sore.
A poem arrives, penned by Ethne herself. She invites you to share her company for a banquet in your honor.

Ethne's banquet was as graceful and beautiful as the queen herself. You longed to stay with the gentle queen, but your restless spirit eventually sent you back to your waiting ship. You look forward to your next meeting.
Faeryl stands shimmering in the moonlight before disappearing into the forest. The Svartalfar are not seen by accident, she must be enticing you to follow her.

Faeryl's seduction is intoxicating. She is as beautiful as the night and her kisses alone are enough to wage war over. Except for the morning requirement to escape from the chains she placed you in while you slept it was a perfect rendezvous.
Even you can't resist feeling intimidated as Hannah brings her warship alongside your galleon. But her offer to meet privately has the whole of the Lanun empire wondering about her desires.
When you wake in the morning Hannah is already gone. She took one of your hats as a souvenir.
The Balseraphs are celebrating for no apparent reason. Keelyn has invited you to join them as a special guest.

You have little memory of your night among the Balseraphs. Back at your ship you drink to nurse a pounding headache and are surprised to find that someone has painted your block and tackle bright white, red and yellow.
Deep within the Doviello lands Mahala celebrates the first snow with a bonfire and brutal contests between her subjects. You are invited to attend.

Mahala is the opposite of her people and you are surprised to find a beautiful woman beneath the war paint and furs. When they are rough she is soft, where they are demanding she is yielding, while their lands are cold her bed is very warm.
I have no time for such dalliances.
Rhoanna requests transport for her and her entourage aboard your flagship.
You find a kindred spirit in the horse maiden and are sorry to see her depart your ship. Are the grasslands of her empire really that different than the rolling seas you call home?

The Clan of Embers celebrate the fall of Bhall by lighting bonfires across their empire. Sheelba, who stands nearly a foot taller than you and is easily twice as strong, invites you to share their celebration and a night hunting with her.
Thessa enters your lands to barter for the Ljosalfar. She asks for a personal tour of your ship.

You had heard rumors that Thessa killed her husband on his wedding night. From her intensity you suspect he died in more active pursuits than as an arcane sacrifice. Fortunately you survived the night better than he did.
The harsh queen of the Amurites is direct about her desires. She has heard about your talents and invites you to her palace so she may judge them herself.
You promise yourself that you will stay away from sorceresses for a while. At one point you would have sworn she transformed into a very affectionate earth elemental.
A gruesome murder has occurred in %s2_city. The town watch found a poor street woman with her throat slit. A killer is loose in the city.
Order the watch to step up patrols.
Pay the assassins' guild to make sure this madman's rampage is ended.
The serial killer has finally been caught in %s2_city. He is a dangerous, deeply disturbed man. It took a dozen guards to subdue him.
Good. Make his execution swift and immediate.
Torture him publicly before his execution.
We need every swordarm we can get, enlist him.
Give him to the keepers of the Asylum until he can better repay his debt.
The killer continues his rampage, people flee the city in fear.

You hear tales of a cave that is guarded by a creature so foul, so cruel that no man yet has fought with it and lived! Bones of full fifty men lie strewn about its lair. They warn that death awaits you with nasty, big, pointy teeth. When your scouts arrive at the cave they find a small white rabbit.
Go on, Bors. Chop his head off!
He's got huge, sharp- eh- he can leap about- look at the bones!
Let us taunt it! It may become so cross that it will make a mistake.
The governor of %s2_city rushes into your throne room. Criminals have kidnapped his daughter and are threatening to kill her if a ransom isn't paid. He claims he is unable to pay what they demand.
It will cost more, but pay adventurers to find and rescue the daughter
A great sage in the city of %s2_city tires of his endless research and wishes to leave our service.
Certainly an expensive study will renew his interest.
Grant him a prestigious position as curator of the library.
Pay to have him trained as an Adept.
He knows too much, have him killed.
Searching the remains of the Sailors' Dirge you find a map to an ancient treasure.

A young woman offers to setup a herbalist shop in %s2_city. Shortly after arriving the %s1_civ_adjective ambassador requests your audience. He describes the woman and says she is a criminal that has fled into your lands. He demands that she be turned over to him.
She sought sanctuary in our lands and we will grant it.
She passed through our lands, but she isn't here any longer. (exile her)
Of course, we will turn her over at once.
The Sheaim have invited our ritualists to participate in their elegy ritual.
We would do well to learn from the Sheaim, send them to the ritual.
What good is our conquest if it is over a world of ashes, ignore their invitation.
They are crazy, send agents to disrupt the ritual.
Your men have discovered a shrine to Camulos, God of War, hidden in the sewers of %s2_city. What would you like them to do?
Do nothing, it is best not to anger the gods.
Order them to destroy the shrine.
Present an offering at the shrine.
An unusual wasting disease has spread in the city of %s2_city . The children seem the strongest hit and the healers warn that many may die if nothing is done.
Ease their suffering and quarantine the city until the disease has passed.
Send an adept proficient in body magic to strengthen their resistance to the disease.

Astrologers report that the Obsidian Scepter has moved into prominence. This constellation is sacred to Aeron and your prophets warn that children born during this time are more likely to be powerful leaders or psychopaths.
Astrologers report that the Great Serpent has moved into prominence. This constellation is sacred to Agares and the sign bodes poorly for goodly nations.
If the King of Hope moves upon Erebus we should honor him. Perform blood rituals in each of our cities.
Astrologers report that the Bow has moved into prominence. This constellation is sacred to Amathaon and your governors report an increase in their cities' birth rates.
I am sure Amathaon signals the birth of a gifted child. Where better to be born than among our people, ask our governors to search for a child that bears Amathaon's mark.
Pray that Amathaon inspires our researchers to greater heights of knowledge.
Astrologers report that the Shroud has moved into prominence. This constellation is sacred to Arawn and it is said to be a good time to visit gravesites and remember those that have passed on.
Astrologers report that the Burnt Wings has moved into prominence. This constellation is sacred to Bhall and your prophets predict it signals the coming of long dry summer.
Astrologers report that the Blazing Sword has moved into prominence. This constellation is sacred to Camulos and your prophets warn against attempting diplomacy during this period.
Astrologers report that the Black Candle has moved into prominence. This constellation is sacred to Ceridwen and your people report a period of strange dreams and visions.
These dreams must lead to someone favored by the Queen of Pain. Make sacrifices to Ceridwen that we might be able to follow her message.
Have our researchers pray to Ceridwen so that they may benefit from her knowledge.
Astrologers report that the Great Tree has moved into prominence. This constellation is sacred to Cernunnos and scouts report animals are more common and aggressive than normal.
That is good. Hold a grand feast in each of our cities.
Astrologers report that the Scales has moved into prominence. This constellation is sacred to Dagda and signals a good period to make agreements and sign treaties.

Astrologers report that the Silver Tears has moved into prominence. This constellation is sacred to Danalin. Your harbormasters report increased catches from fishing fleets and your governors report an increase in suicides.
Hold festivals in the cities and allow the wine and oblivio to flow freely.
Astrologers report that the Jeweled Mask has moved into prominence. This constellation is sacred to Esus and your watch commanders report increased criminal behavior after its display.
Certainly our people will delight in this sign.
Astrologers report that the Shield of Valor has moved into prominence. This constellation is sacred to Junil and marks a rise in his power within the world.
This is an auspicious time indeed, have our garrisons form parades through the cities in Junil's honor.
Astrologers report that the Sleeping Dragon has moved into prominence. This constellation is sacred to Kilmorph and your governors report an increase in mine production.
Hold ceremonies in the temples. But don't spend too much.

Astrologers report that the Night Sun has moved into prominence. This constellation is sacred to Lugus and is so bright that some nights are almost as bright as day. Criminals' activities are hampered by the light.
Open the council halls to the people. All should witness and be enlightened by this event.
Astrologers report that the Coin has moved into prominence. This constellation is sacred to Mammon and your governors report an increase in commerce and crime during this period.
Astrologers report that the Bear has moved into prominence. This constellation is sacred to Mulcarn and some say it signals the coming of a fierce winter.
This is the sign of the return of our glory.
Astrologers report that the Eye of Heaven has moved into prominence. This constellation is sacred to Nantosuelta and most believe it signals an auspicious time to plan marriages.
Astrologers report that the Open Tome has moved into prominence. This constellation is sacred to Oghma and your researchers make significant progress during this period.
Astrologers report that the Bronze Owl has moved into prominence. This constellation is sacred to Sirona and your prophets predict that it signals a coming period of peace and happiness.

Astrologers report that the Arms of God has moved into prominence. This constellation is sacred to Sucellus and your healers report sudden, and often miraculous, recovery from diseases among your people.
Astrologers report that the Pegasus has moved into prominence. This constellation is sacred to Tali and strong storms rage across your lands.
A slave has escaped from your lands.
An angry slave has taken up arms against you.

The captain finds an illegal slave ring within the city. The male slaves were forced to fight in underground tournaments, the women suffered far worse. The captain requests your permission to execute the traders and free the slaves.
Congratulate the captain on his work and approve his request.
That seems like a waste of perfectly good slaves...
The guard captain of %s2_city suspects that there is an illegal slave ring operating in the city and requests additional funds to track them down.
There are more important things to focus on.
The guard captain of %s2_city reports growing smuggling activity and wants to know how to proceed.
Do nothing, their activity stimulates the economy of the city
Run them out of the city, they invite crime

Moaning sobs float through the gray streets of %s2_city, filling its citizens with sadness. The sounds flow from a dark, two-storey townhouse. The home appears abandoned and guards are unable to find the source of the crying.
There is little we can do.
Send an adept who is proficient with spirit magic to calm the spirit.
Delightful, begin charging admission to the home.
The people of %s2_city want to rule themselves under Minister Koun, a local politician. They would remain a part of our empire, but become sovereign in their own matters.
Giant spiders have nested in a local mine. How should we respond?
Pay some adventurers to deal with them.
Don't risk them feeding on our people, collapse the mine.
Order the people away from the mine, I will send in soldiers to deal with the spiders.

Your advisors report that your agricultural advisor has been acting strangely. She has been painting the cows to see if it influences milk production and planting corn on rooftops to keep the foxes from getting into it. They say something must be done.
Her experiments may be expensive but I encourage radical thinking among my advisors.
Shes lost her mind, assign a new agriculture advisor.
Fire the complaining advisors, she's the only one doing it right.

The %s1_civ_adjective ambassador pleads for your help. You have already made your people into the most powerful empire on Erebus. He would like you leave your people and become the leader of their empire.
No, I will remain the leader of my people.
Yes, I will lead your pathetic nation out of its squalor.
Your traits have changed (mouseover your flag to see your new traits).
The governor of %s2_city reports finding documents detailing a plan to overthrow the city. The creator of the documents is unknown but the governor suspects it is from your own citizenry.
Ignore them, the loyalty of my people is beyond question.
Order all local militia to begin a search of the city, question every citizen and search every house.
Invite the people to a feast, a thinning is required. (requires the Calabim civilization)
No, we will keep the resources we have.
A dwarven adept has discovered the secret of turning Gold into Copper. He asks if you would like to hire him to transform your local vein of Gold into Copper?
Yes, we could use the Copper to make weapons for our units.
A dwarven adept has discovered the secret of turning Copper into Gold. He asks if you would like to hire him to transform your local vein of Copper into Gold?
Yes, we could use the Gold to fill our vaults.
An old pirate offers to sell you his only item of value, a map to treasure buried long ago.
It seems a reasonable price, we will take it.
No, why trade gold I have now for gold I have to send men across the world for?
A two-headed cow has been born in your lands. Your people are unsure what it means and they come to you for advice.
The Undercouncil has offered additional support to your empire.
Request that some Undercouncil investigators be stationed in your empire.
Allow the Undercouncil to train your recon units.
Send your scholars to learn from the Undercouncil researchers.

Fishermen share a legend of an ancient people, called the Aifons, that breathed water and air. These people were destroyed during the Age of Magic though the cause of that destruction is unknown. The legend says that their ancient homeland, a distant island, remains and may be the home of some lost treasure, or the force that destroyed them.
There are legends of a tunnel that stretches from creation to the lands of the dead. It is known as Bradeline's Well and no one knows what treasures or nightmares exist within it.

Long ago Kylorin is said to have locked Barbatos, the head of the School of Necromancy, in his own Sepulcher. Explorers report that they may have found that legendary site, but the massive stone that held the Sepulcher closed has been broken in two.

Your people speak of a great stone figure that is carved into the mountainside. They warn against going too close to the figure as powerful creatures roost in the caves around the mountain. Old maps claim that the figure used to be on another mountain entirely, leading many to speculate that from time to time the Guardian may arise and wander about on its own.
Your scouts report that you may be close to Letum Frigus, the ancient battleground where Kylorin defeated the God of Winter. Surely our nation should lay claim to such a legendary site.
Your scouts return with evidence that Letum Frigus, the last place Mulcarn was seen on Erebus, may lay nearby. If we can make a pilgrimage to that site it will embolden our people.

Rumors tell of a great temple to Bhall, whose top burns with a fire fueled by the corpses of the angels that stood against her when she fell. Your people demand that this abomination, the Pyre of the Seraphic, be destroyed.
Veil worshipers in %s2_city threaten to burn down a Temple of the Order.
Order the local militia to help burn down the temple

A volcanic explosion shakes the surrounding countryside. Smoke rises from the fractured mountain peak. Fortunately no one was injured in the blast, but your people wonder how long they will remain safe in the shadow of the volcano.
There is evidence that one of our regiments has been torturing prisoners. They argue that they use the prisoners in their war games, to make it more exciting and more realistic for their men.
Congratulate the unit commander for his ferocity.

Decius returns home and spends a night feasting and telling tales with the men of his Father's holdings. Rosier's parting words haunt him, however, and he retires early. From under his bed comes an inky black snake, hissing and swaying as it crawls up him. Decius tries to grab it but cannot move, and the snake speaks to him. "Noble one... you serve loyally and unquestioningly. How is your service repaid? Such a hard life. Surely such skill and valor as yours should be better rewarded. You deserve power and wealth beyond your station. Is honor such a dear currency to you?"[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Finally Decius finds his voice. "Away!" He reaches for the snake, but it slithers away, under his bed. Decius reaches for it, finally grasping the thing and strangling it with his bare hands until...[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Until he awakes to his father's voice. "Are you alright my son... Decius, by god, what are you doing?"[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Decius is on his knees with his hands wrapped around an octopus-headed idol which glows faintly in the dark.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"I had a nightmare. A demon was tempting me, and..."[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"And it looks to me like you gave in. I would have never thought you capable of this blasphemy. But nor would I have suspected Rosier, either. We shall leave this for the Confessors to determine."[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"I have seen how the Order judges, and would ask you to trust your own judgment. Trust your own son!"[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"I must rather trust my own eyes, Decius."[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"Then I guess I must trust my feet, Lord Commander." Decius swung, smacking his father with the idol. His father staggered back, and Decius rushed past, heading for the stables before alarm could be given.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]He was a fugitive, which is almost as bad as a confession. He would have no succor within the Empire. And the Empire's reach was well beyond its borders-forts lie north, east, and south. And to the west lie the Lanun. He almost stopped. He believed in law, in order, he had sworn his life to the unending crusade against evil. A hundred times he had risked that life on the field of battle. But he would not die the heretic's death, reviled and anathematized.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]The diviners would not look at his valorous history, nor could they what had actually happened. They would look into his heart, and read any doubt as disloyalty.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]He spurred his horse toward the west.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]When he arrived in Innsmouth there was a ship heading across the great sea, carrying spices, furs, and slaves. He was recognized as their enemy-but not, to his luck, as their commander. His horse, and the bit of gold he had in her saddlebag bought him one way passage, no questions asked. Or just one question.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"We go to the desert of Myrh, Bannorman. We can let you off with the Calabim, or you can hire a guide to take you to a Malakim city. What is your choice?"[NEWLINE][NEWLINE](The civilization you choose will determine what civilization you play as in future scenarios)
I will go to the Calabim. Better to hide where the so-called righteous fear to tread. Among the feared Calabim I can make my way less encumbered by the laws that have bound me to now.
I will go to the Malakim. I cannot turn my back on my beliefs, even if the land that I served has wronged me. Among the honest Malakim perhaps I can find some solace.
The priests were wrong, Rosier argued. "I used the forbidden power and am neither tainted nor possessed. I am as much my own man as I ever was, if not more."
Rosier, you have broken your vows, submit to the confessor and face trial.
Rosier rides off before you can stop him, he curses you as yet another puppet who has confused courage with obedience.
I see no evil here, but you have transgressed the word of a Confessor. You will not be welcome here and I cannot take you in.
Rosier clasps your hand. "Perhaps there is some hope for the Order," he says before mounting his horse and fleeing the Bannor lands.

The wall to the south has deep grooves around the edges, it looks to be a hidden door. Do you want to open up?
Yes, let's see what lies beyond.
An emissary for Judecca requests audience with you. He offers peace if you only declare war against the %s1_player.

Lethe haunts your dreams. She claims that your %s3_unit seeks eternal rest but resists due to loyalty to you. If you would allow that unit to sacrifice itself Lethe would show her favor by making peace between your nations.

An apparition appears in your throne room, it is the glorious Meresin. He smiles down at you and, claiming extreme benevolence, offers peace between his armies and your own. The only price he asks is the slightest act of supplication, that you would kiss his feet.
I came to purge this land of devils, not make deals with them.
Lord Ouzza praises your strength. He offers peace between his army and our own if we are willing to celebrate that peace by sacrificing some of the citizens of each of our cities to his glory.

The shadow of Duke Sallos himself falls over your bed. He is dark, powerful and beautiful. He offers you peace in exchange for that which he desires most, a night of carnal pleasure between the two of you.

You wake up to find a succubus in the service of Duke Sallos floating above your bed. She is dark and beautiful. She whispers to you, offering peace with her lord if you are willing to consummate the agreement with the most intimate of acts.
A beetle shaped demon approaches under the banner of Statius. He offers peace with his lord in exchange for the city of %s2_city.
I will pay your price, we will have peace. At least for a time.

Amelanchier is defeated and your troops capture him fleeing the smoking remains of his capital. Your huntresses bind him and bring him to your camp. Amelanchier refuses to speak or acknowledge the power of the winter court. Distant howls interrupt your decision, and it is followed by a pack of wolves, half-wolves and beastmen entering your camp. Baron Duin Halfmorn leads them, and he makes a single request.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"I offer my alliance if you give me Amelanchier, I wish to add him to my pack."
No, have Amelanchier jailed. He deserves better than a military execution.
No, kill him. I'd rather have elven blood spilt on the grass than tainted by beasts.
Do with him as you will. The wolves will make powerful allies.

Rivanna is defeated and many of your hunters are killed trying to capture her. Now she stands before you, bound and under close guard. But just as you are about to give your verdict the shadows seem to stretch and consume the chamber. A beautiful human woman stands at the heart of the shadows, Alexis of the Calabim.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"I have come to entreat for the life of Rivanna, she would be more fitting as a dark queen. I can offer the loyalty of the Calabim in exchange."
No, she will have the compassion of the summer court. We will hold a trial for her crimes.
There is only one response to treason, kill her.
The friendship of the Calabim is appreciated, Rivanna is yours.

Thessa is defeated and many of your hunters are killed trying to capture her. Some say an angel stood protectively over her, but if it is true that angel is gone now. Now Thessa stands before you, bound and under close guard. But just as you are about to give your verdict the shadows seem to stretch and consume the chamber. A beautiful human woman stands at the heart of the shadows, Alexis of the Calabim.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"I have come to entreat for the life of Thessa, she would be more fitting as a dark queen. I can offer the loyalty of the Calabim in exchange."
No, Thessa is deluded by the Summer queen but she will be imprisoned for her crimes.
Thessa has been apart from her husband for too long, allow them to remeet in the afterworld.
Accept her with the regards of the winter queen. We look forward to improved relations with the Calabim.

Volanna is defeated and your troops capture her fleeing the smoking remains of her capital. Your huntresses bind her and bring her to your camp. Volanna refuses to speak or acknowledge the power of the winter court. Distant howls interrupt your decision, and it is followed by a pack of wolves, half-wolves and beastmen entering your camp. Baron Duin Halfmorn leads them, and he makes a single request.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"I offer my alliance if you give me Volanna, I wish to add her to my pack."
No, she will have the compassion of the summer court. We will hold a trial for her crimes.
There is only one response to treason, kill her.
We accept the brotherhood of the wolves, Volanna is yours to do with as you will.

One of your aides, a young elven hunter named Parith approaches you in private. With some moderate financing he offers to head out of the Umbrawood and seek a country that may be sympathetic to your cause. How do you respond?
No, we will win our own war.
Very well, take what you need and go quickly.
Which civilization would you like to lead this city? This will control the type of units and buildings that can be produced here.
I've been playing this clown's game for too long. Together you and I could overthrow him, take the boats you need and I will aid you in your war. It's better than playing puppets to a madman!

Don't always promote a unit as soon as it is possible. It may be wise to wait and see what kinds of units your opponent has before using up a promotion. Also, wounded units heal some damage when a promotion is used.
Unescorted settlers or galleons-or especially highly promoted mages-are all huge risks. Make sure you are willing to take them!
Barbarians can appear anywhere a tile is obscured by fog of war, or on unexplored lairs, so never assume a tile you can't see is safe, even if you checked it the turn before.
Check the foreign advisor often-knowing what your friends (and foes) can offer in trade is valuable information.

Be careful in signing Open Border agreements-make sure your "friend" isn't mapping out your land for sale to the highest bidder! Also be aware that civilizations under the Council of Esus religion will be able to declare war without having their units removed from their rivals' lands.
Beware of Barbarians in the early stages of the game. Orthus, the Barbarian King is really strong, but the unit who defeats him receives his axe as a reward.
If you find a valuable resource that is too far away for you to use, it may still be smart to keep a unit on top of it, if only to find out who eventually is going to control it.
Don't neglect cottages! They may start small, but once they mature, you will be glad you built them.

Take advantage of the opportunity to pillage a cottage improvement. The time required to advance each level of growth for a cottage can't be hurried, and the gold you get for pillaging them is considerable, especially if you have the Raiders trait.

When trying to capture a mature city, bring plenty of siege weapons. You will want to bombard the defenses and to soften up the defenders. If you don't have siege available, fireball-casting mages make a good substitute.

Be aware of the strengths and weaknesses of units. For example, Crossbowmen and Longbowmen get a bonus when defending cities, while assassins and marksmen will attack the weakest combat unit in a stack. Phalanxes excel at conquering cites, while Berserkers cause collateral damage.
Don't be afraid to attack with ranged units-archers and longbowmen may not be the best offensive units, but properly promoted, they can do a respectable job.
The Flanking promotion only allows a unit to withdraw when near death, so it may help to leave these units a movement point to run away to safety if they do withdraw from an attack.

Consider keeping one unit with the Medic promotion in every large stack-the bonus isn't cumulative, but it can make the difference in keeping an advance going. Disciple class units are the only ones who begin with this promotion, and no one else can learn it. (The Grigori Civilization can build medics instead.)
All religions are different and give different benefits, so choose carefully.

Watch for announcements about religions being founded and wonders being completed-this can give you a hint as to how advanced your foes are. Should you build the Eyes and Ears network wonder you will be able to see what your rivals research.
If you choose to have a state religion, work diligently to spread it to all your cities. Some civics such as God King and Theology give extra benefits in cities where your state religion is present.

Open Borders agreements are invitations for your missionaries-spread your state religion quickly and take advantage of the Shrine benefits if you control the Holy City. If your religion spreads widely enough, your neighbors may convert to your faith, which can boost relations.
Make sure you need every building your city creates. Cities bringing in no commerce can sometimes skip Libraries, just as a city that will never see battle can skip Palisades and Walls.
There is no limit to the amount of National Wonders you can have per city. Still, you will want to consider carefully before deciding which city you want to build them in.
When facing a tough defender with weak units, bring overwhelming numbers. If your target survives the battle, it will have gained experience and then it will become even more dangerous!
A good time to check for trading possibilities with another civilization is right after researching a new technology-shop around and see what you can get for it before others beat you to it.
Beware spreading The Order religion to a city with the Ashen Veil religion-the followers of these religions are not prone to peaceful coexistence.

Locate and acquire different resources. While Copper can be used for moderate improvement to melee units, Iron will give a more substantial bonus once unlocked and you will need Mithril to have the strongest melee units.

A city's population growth is halted while training settlers and workers. In some cases, it may be better to let a city grow before training these units. The Luchuirp Mud Golems are an exception to this, and Infernal cities will never expand on their own.

Wars are rarely won in a day. If you lack the force to capture enemy cities, consider pillaging the countryside instead. You may lure your opponent's units out of their strongholds. Even if it doesn't lure your enemy out, a war of attrition may lead to economic advantage, and ultimately to your victory.

Some techs can be discovered only if you have the appropriate state religion. For example, only Ashen Veil nations can research Infernal Pact. The Fellowship of the Leaves, Octopus Overlords and Runes of Kilmorph also have an exclusive technology.
Grains, livestock, and seafood not only provide resources, but also rich yields to the local city. Cities planted near two or more of these food sources will grow quickly!
Explore your region! Discover what types of resources you have nearby, and plan your research paths to enable you to hook up these resources sooner rather than later.
If your enemy is too strong to tackle in the field, hide behind your city walls and buy time. Build unit types and choose promotions that will best counter the forces aligned against you.
Bigger is not always better. Overexpansion can stifle your economy and your research, even while it adds to your population and production.
Guard your experienced units! A veteran unit with older weaponry can often defeat a new unit with more advanced equipment.
A civilization without currency cannot build a specialized economy nor support a growing empire.
Wonders of the World not only provide unique benefits, they also inspire your populace. More great people will appear in cities that build ancient wonders or multiple great wonders.

There are many ways to make your people happy: with religion, with luxurious resources, with city improvements, with civics, with culture rate. If you lack opportunities in some areas, focus your attention on the others. Avoid having angry citizens whenever possible!

Paladins are special units only available to Good nations. Similarly, only nations with an Evil alignment can train Eidolons, and Druids are restricted to Neutral. Alignment is displayed by score and modified by religion.
The Fawns are costly units in the beginning of the game, but they do not require any special buildings or resources-just the Fellowship of the Leaves religion present in the city.
When a Diseased unit attacks or defends, it can Disease units on the tile of its opponent.
Diseased or Plagued units have lower healing rates, so they may never heal if there is no unit with Medic promotion nearby.
Only Mary Morbus and Yersinia can spread the plague. Yersinia is a Barbarian hero; Mary Morbus may be given to a player who has built an Alchemy Lab.
Immortals are reborn in the owner's capital after dying, with all their experience and promotions, but only once per turn. To kill Immortals forever you must kill them twice in a single turn.
The Blood of the Phoenix wonder gives the Immortal promotion to all your units. These units will be reborn in your capital if killed, but they lose this promotion after they are reborn.
New civics are not always better civics! Don't switch automatically. Weigh your options; consider your needs and priorities.
Units killed by werewolves might become werewolves too. Ravenous Werewolves become stronger when they kill living units, but if they don't feed soon they will abandon you.
The Runes of Kilmorph religion increases gold income in cities where it spreads. The Ashen Veil religion increases research in cities where it spreads.
The Vitalize spell transforms deserts and tundras to plains, and plains to grasslands.
The Bloom spell can create forests.

The Genesis ritual improves every tile in your current empire. Deserts and tundras become plains, plains becomes grasslands, jungles becomes forests and forests grow on every free tile. It is a one-time action.
The Hero promotion gives the unit 1 XP per turn until it reaches 100 XP.
There is a minimum of 10 turns between civic changes.
Civilizations with the Slavery civic convert 25% of the units they defeat into Slaves.
Some civics are only enabled when you have the required state religion. These are often very powerful.
Some units can be trained only if you have the required state religion. You can't train Crusaders without the Order religion, and you can't train Satyrs without the Fellowship of the Leaves religion.

Balance your research. Spending too much time on advanced techs leads to long research times. Neglecting cheaper, older technologies can cost you. But don't overlook the advantage of having a powerful unit early.
The best way to maintain peace is to control a significant army. Other civilizations will prey on weak neighbors, but if you are strong enough they may look elsewhere for targets.
Civilizations with the Organized trait can build Command Posts even without Great Commanders. Other nations must use Great Commanders to construct them.
The Bless enchantment lasts until the end of the unit's first combat.
Each World Unit can be created only once. If such a unit dies, it can not be recreated. Heroes and Apocalypse units are World Units.
The Mithril Golem and Meshabber of Dis are Avatars. They are enormously strong, but not invulnerable. It's possible to kill them, just very difficult.
Apocalypse kills 60% of all living units and halves population in all cities.
Mages' Fireballs cause collateral damage and can bombard city defenses. Fireballs will not be affected by the Summoner trait.
An Adept's Haste spell affects all living units in the same tile. It lasts for 1 turn.

Spellcasters only have access to spells in spheres their civilization has the mana for. So you need Fire mana if you want your spellcasters to learn Fire spells. Four technologies give Arcane class units the ability to build mana nodes of different types. This is permanent unless you have a Mage with the Dispel spell, granted by Metamagic, which is buildable after researching Sorcery.
Units cost money in maintenance-don't use fifty when fifteen will do.
Don't think your heroes are invincible-they can have an impressive list of promotions, but their raw power is not too great. Late game units can overpower middle game heroes in direct combat.
Most units require special buildings. Some buildings improve all units of certain type. Do not try to build all possible buildings in every city-specialize your cities.
The fire aura of Meshabber of Dis will damage your units as well as your enemies'. Damaging another civilization's units is considered an act of war.
If the Armageddon Counter gets too high the Avatar of Wrath will enter the world as a Barbarian unit, and a percentage of the world's living units will join him.
Blight will strike all players as the Armageddon Counter rises. It gives a large health penalty to every city and damages every unit.
Soldiers of Kilmorph and Slaves can hurry production in cities.
Disciples can make a little culture burst in a city. Priests can construct temples of their religions.
The Great Commander can be joined to a unit. Doing so will increase the unit's strength and cause it to gain xp faster. Great Commanders can be split from the unit at any point.

Erebus is a dangerous world; most scouts don't return from exploring and building more cities than you can defend will often doom your empire. Exploring a dungeon or lair, especially an epic dungeon with a unique name, has the potential to make things much more dangerous for those nearby.
With the Conquest civic you receive more gold when you capture a city, but the city loses extra population.
Never despair in the face of a large stack of units. A Mage's Fireball may not be strong, but it can do a lot of damage to an enemy stack. If you have no mages-use Catapults.
You may want to choose a religion others share for the diplomatic bonus, or go your own path to have less competition for religious heroes.

Recon units can be promoted with Subdue Animal to capture animals once the Animal Husbandry tech is researched. These can be used to attack or added to cities to boost happiness and culture. But act fast, animals won't spawn for long!
Razing cities and spreading the Ashen Veil religion will raise the Armageddon Counter. This will lead to apocalyptic events and increased aggression.

Sometimes landmarks will spawn when the map is created. These are unique improvements that are markers of events from ages past. They will often give great tile yields from the start, or other special abilities. Do what you can to control these tiles, but be sure you know what they do. Building a city near the fertile Yggdrasil is a great boon, while building near the Guardian of Pristinus Pass is quite risky.
Rushing production with population is only available with the Slavery civic, which is available at Way of the Wicked.

Priests can learn the Command promotion, to have a chance of converting living enemy units that they defeat. After upgrading to high priests they can take subsequent command promotions. Command IV is only available to High Priests of the Order.
Religious heroes will abandon you if you change religions. Demagogs will do so if you leave the Crusade civic, and Royal Guard units will leave if you change from the Aristocracy civic.
The arrival of the Infernal civilization will also begin transforming the world into hell. Work to lower the Armageddon Counter if you want to keep this from spreading to your lands.
All players who learn a religion-founding tech will receive a disciple of that religion, though only the first gets the benefits of a Holy City.
Each Civilization has distinct benefits and drawbacks. The Grigori, for example, cannot adopt a state religion-but watch out for their many heroes!

Not every city can occupy an ideal location. Some cities can be placed to acquire resources or make use of marginal terrain. Keep an eye on your cities' maintenance costs, so that you do not expand too quickly and stifle your economy.
Elven Workers (and Slaves) can build Cottages, Farms, and Plantations on top of forests. This is extremely useful for extra production and health.
Hidden Nationality units, such as animals, can attack without declaring war.
Some leaders have the Adaptive trait. This will allow their player to choose a new trait periodically. Plan ahead to be Aggressive or Raiders during war and Financial or Philosophical during peace.

There are more options for victory. Religious requires using diplomacy - and inquisitors - to spread a religion you control far and wide. To build the Tower of Mastery, you must control a diverse assortment of mana, and the Altar of the Luonnotar can give the win to those who gain lots of Great Prophets.
Adjust the game options to fit the play experience you want, such as no Armageddon Counter, more animals - or even a world already filled with barbarian cities!

A leader with the Barbarian trait has nothing to fear from the orcs that seek to ravage other players' lands, though they must still contend with animals. Use this to your advantage, but beware, if your score grows too much higher than your rivals your peace with the barbarians will end.

Unless turned off, random events will strike players based partly on their in-game actions. Often the options you have to react to these opportunities depend on your state religion, buildings present, or gold on hand.

Exploration is vital not only to search for tribal villages and resources to settle near, but to find monster lairs such as barrows and ruins. Destroy these as soon as you can - unless, perhaps, if they are nearer to your rivals than to you.

The Mercurian and Infernal civilizations are not of the mortal world, so you cannot begin play as either. But if you call them into the world you will be given the option to play as these powerful civilizations. Call the Infernals by researching Infernal Pact; the Mercurians can be brought in by building the Mercurian Gate wonder.

There are thousands of different kinds of dungeons spread across Erebus, some abandoned with forgotten treasures available for the taking, others are the lairs for dark creatures. The only way to tell the difference between the two is to explore them.

Although normally goblins aren't strong enough to pose a real threat to armies the Scorpion Clan goblins have two advantages that allow them to claim their land. First they are organized better than other goblin tribes, and the only ones to build fortifications in the wilderness. And secondly is the greasy poison they coat their weapons with. The creation of the poison is a secret of the Scorpion Clan shamans, and so far the secret has been well kept.

Casting Raise Skeleton on a graveyard will grant you 3 skeletons. Casting Sanctify on a graveyard grants a free Law Bringer. Robbing a graveyard produces random results. Casting Resurrection in a graveyard produces a free Champion.
Beware the Guardian of Pristin Pass, foul creatures roost in its alcoves and they are likely to swoop down on those who come too close to the stone giant.
Spawns demons if it isn't eliminated.

There is nothing left here but echoes of the battles that have been fought here. This is where Kylorin met Mulcarn in the final battle that killed a god. Wild men live in the caves around the site and claim that someday their god will return.
Spawns lions if it isn't eliminated.
Ships do well to avoid the swirling Maelstrom, though sailors claim ships that pass through it often come out on seas in different parts of the world.

When in great need the Malakim seek guidance by heading alone into the desert. Though they risk death they often receive visions or enlightenment. The most holy of these wildlands is the Mirror of Heaven, a desert so hot the sands have melted to a smooth glass sea.

The totems are said to be manufactured in hell itself and planted here in Erebus as a sign of hell's growing power. Regardless of their origin their effect is felt by any that come near, an overpowering fear that sends even the bravest running away from the totem

When the gods met at the seven pines they called a truce in the Godswar. The divine armies withdrew to their sacred lands and humanity had a hint of the peaceful times that would come. But the greatest of Aeron's angels, the archangel Odio, ignored his lord's command. He was given over to his bloodlust and led an army of Ira into the lands of Kilmorph.[PARAGRAPH:1]"What means the words of one who does not rule his own home? If Aeron is to share our council he must withdraw his ara from Odio"[PARAGRAPH1:]The gods agreed with Kilmorph and Aeron's protection was removed from the raging Odio, in that instant the queen of gems reached out and pulled Odio into the earth. There she left him transformed to stone, eternal testament to the power of the gods and the cost of defying their will.

Chapter 1: Fall of Mammon Cycle[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Mammon sat in the shadow of a great mountain. He liked creation, the smells of fresh earth and growing things, the mix of warm sunlight and cool breezes. But a world is more than the material and his mind was exploring one of his own creations, mathematics.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]The One had removed the power of creation from them, but the gods were still powerful. Though the laws of Erebus were set, they could easily bend them. But in time they would return to their natural state. Mammon wished he could remake some of the laws he had applied, and even now played with changing them and watched the impact of his changes on the clouds that drifted overhead. The way the clouds split, funneled, dispersed and moved were minutely changed by the slightest of his adjustments.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]As the god of foresight Mammon watched the world play out due to his tiny changes. The clouds shadow that uncovered a mother mouse a second sooner. The hawk that spotted the now uncovered mouse. The mouse that would die in the hawks claws. The mouse babies that would starve without their mother. The seeds that would not be eaten by the mice. The plants that would now grow from those seeds.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]The clouds rolled towards the west, they were bone white and hung low in the sky. All except a single cloud that traveled east, seemingly ignoring all natural laws. Mammon considered the futures changed by the defiant cloud. Weather patterns changed, storms that would and wouldn't occur now. The changed world that existed because of that cloud.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"Would you be so quick to change everything if you knew the implications of your actions?" Mammon asked the sky.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Tali, god of the air, smiled down at the serious god, "I suspect that everything turns out the same no matter what we do."[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Mammon frowned, "That is not true."[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]But secretly Mammon wondered if Tali was right.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]A distant ceremony beckoned to both the gods. All the gods gathered around a shallow pool and with a thought Mammon and Tali joined them.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Within the pool a woman floated, perfect of form with smooth, pale skin and long, black hair. She was to be Gabella, formed by Aeron into the first woman and she was receiving a blessing from each of the gods.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Bhall, goddess of fire, floated in the pool with Gabella and fire danced across the pools surface and shimmered in its depths. Bhall held the sleeping Gabella and whispered into her ear, "I give you the capacity for passion and love, that you can give these gifts to others and can receive them to yourself."[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]At that she kissed Gabella gently on the forehead. Gabella continued to float as Bhall let go and stepped out of the pool. Ceridwen came next, floating above the pool she allowed the long tendrils of her gown to reach down and lift Gabella gently to her.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Oghma was watching Mammon closely. The two were as close as their precepts, Oghma was knowledge of everything that was and Mammon was the god of knowledge of everything that will be. The thin line of the present separated their dominions and because of that the gods had a close affinity for each other.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Deciding that something had changed Oghma whispered to Mammon, "You seem bothered."[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Nemed spoke to all the gathered gods before Mammon could respond.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"I mean to give her eternal life. That mankind can share our immortality and live without death."[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]The gods considered, all life in creation was meant to be temporary. They were not making gods, but a world with seasons and cycles. Arawn was the first to respond.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"They have not known heaven, but they will yearn for it. Are you sure that our creation is so perfect that it should be unending?"[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]At that the gods all began speaking at once. Only Agares, who watched without comment, and Mammon stayed out of the conversation. Mammon already knew the outcome. It was the same as any major decision they had to make, they would ask him. It was Nemed who asked.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"Mammon, what do you foresee for Gabella and her children? Should she live eternal, or live only for a time within creation?"[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]For the first time Mammon was afraid to answer. Something was wrong, and for one who always knew the future being blind to it terrified him. Mammon could see the creation of Gabella, could see her rebellion and refusal to submit to the plan of the gods. Beyond that he saw the rebellion of Agares, and his attempt to challenge the One. He saw the One standing in creation, judging the world. But he couldn't see anything beyond that moment. If there was any future beyond that he was blind to it. Mammon suspected that the One unmade them and creation. He suspected that he was seeing his own death.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]In regards to Gabella's immortality, for the time that Mammon could see there was no difference. With or without eternal life Gabella would refuse to become the mother of humanity. With either option she would live until Mammon's vision failed him. She would live as long as Mammon would.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Rather than admit that his vision was gone, rather than tell the gods that Agares would betray them, that they would all die, Mammon pretended to know and for the first time gave advice without knowing if it was correct.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"Allow them to be immortal, they should not fear death." Mammon was beginning to know that fear to well himself.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Arawn seemed bothered by the response but said nothing. Nemed entered the pool, embraced Gabella and whispered into her ear. From that moment she was as immortal as a single god could make her.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Mammon was next. He walked across the surface of the pool and sat down at Gabella's side.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"Wake child." He said softly.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Gabella sat up and her eyes fluttered open. She was still in the daze of birth and likely wouldn't see or remember him, but he wanted to see her eyes. Aeron had fashioned her body perfectly, she was beautiful, strong and unique in feature.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"I give you..." Mammon leaned close, so that no one could overhear, "I give you nothing, so that you might always wonder and won't know the pleasures and the pains of the future."[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Gabella lay back down in the pool and returned to her sleep. Agares was the last to give his blessing and he stepped into the pool. At his touch the water changed to a blend of black and gold, a beautiful labyrinth or bright gold veins appearing and disappearing into emptiness. The gold strands caressed Gabella's body and again her eyes fluttered open to meet Agares's gaze.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"I give you hope, a belief in what can be, that you will not know despair."[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Oghma was watching Mammon closely, he would be the only one who knew that Mammon didn't give a gift to Gabella. Similarly Mammon watched Agares, searching unsuccessfully for some hint of his future betrayal.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE][LINK=SPELL_ESCAPE]Chapter 2: Fall of Mammon Cycle[\LINK][NEWLINE][LINK=IMPROVEMENT_SEVEN_PINES]Chapter 3: Fall of Mammon Cycle[\LINK][NEWLINE][LINK=BUILDING_ALTAR_OF_THE_LUONNOTAR]Chapter 4: Fall of Mammon Cycle[\LINK]

In the frozen wastes explorers have reported seeing a beautiful glow in the night sky. There have been many stories about the source of this glow, the passing of spirits from this world to the next, the shimmering of the sleeping sun, the remains of Mulcarn himself.[PARAGRAPH:1]But the truth is that far into the wastes there exists a ring of starlight, the Ring of Carcer. And trapped within is Brigit, the archangel of Bhall whom Bhall was unwilling to kill in her fall. Those seeking evidence that the queen of fire is not completely lost to the whispers of Agares cite her preservation of Brigit as their evidence. Others say that if Brigit can be freed she could kill Bhall and claim her dominion for herself. And we would once again have a goddess of holy fire.[PARAGRAPH:1]But these are only stories, shared on cold snowy nights. For there is none so far who is capable of passing through the Ring of Carcer and freeing the trapped archangel.

[TAB]Adopted daughter of Os-Gabella and elder sister of Flauros, Alexis is the queen and first of the vampires. Raised by an immortal mother, she was faced with her own mortality and unwilling to accept that she would be the first in the Bair of Lacuna to die. To get her over her fear of death, Os-Gabella took her to the crude villages of early men and showed her how they lived and died. Wishing to examine this death more closely, Alexis came to the village at night and killed a shepherd.[PARAGRAPH:1]The shepherd's death didn't answer her questions: she saw no spirit leaving his body and his body grew cool, but if his life went anywhere she couldn't see the change. Alexis had access to the teaching of Ceridwen, who had built the Bair of Lacuna and had surrounded it in runes that keep the unwelcome from entering it from other planes, and those imprisoned within it from leaving through the same means. These last runes Alexis used at the site of her 2nd killing, a young acolyte of Lugus named Lanthis.[PARAGRAPH:1]Lanthis lay dying but unable to die within Alexis's ring of runes, his spirit unable to escape to the vault. Cut and battered within the circle, Lanthis writhed in agony while Alexis watched. When she tired of watching, Alexis stepped into the circle and allowed Lanthis's spirit an escape, into her. To transition the spirit she touched him, kissing him on his blood soaked forehead. At that moment, at that taste of blood, the first vampire was born. Alexis didn't become possessed by the spirit, she consumed it and her mortal life was extended because of it.[PARAGRAPH:1]Over the next few centuries, she shared the secret with her brother and they parted from their immortal mother and began hunting men in a variety of guises. One life could extend their own for 20-30 years so they didn't hunt often but they were a legendary threat to men from creation.

"Do we turn back, my liege?" he asked.[PARAGRAPH:1]Arturus shook his head. "No, we cannot. This is too important. But break camp, we'll get no more sleep tonight."[PARAGRAPH:2]The rest of the journey was calm enough, though Arturus grew nervous for reasons of his own as they reached their destination. [TAB]Following visions and dreams, Auric stumbled across the frozen wastes, his companions left forgotten or dead behind him. [TAB]Cardith truly was a remarkable monarch, Gilcrass reflected as he watched the Boy-King play a game of chess with one of his advisors. This had a simple explanation: Cardith was, as far as anyone could tell, an orphan. He had no family history and no-one recognized him as hailing from any famous noble families. Men and women, orcs and elves, children and adults, all caught in their own grey worlds.[PARAGRAPH:1]I talked to the spirit of a man who had been killed by an order Confessor for lying, a boy who had starved because his family couldn't afford food and the teachings of Kilmorph don't emphasize charity, an elf who had used wood from a sacred tree to rebuild his home and had been killed by the Fellowship for it. And thousands who had died in wars they didn't believe in for gods they didn't trust and who didn't accept them.[PARAGRAPH:1]Later I went back to Cassiel, he was sitting alone on the roof of his palace.[PARAGRAPH:1]"Are we forever doomed to this in-between place? "The places they have made are not heaven, the true heaven is closed to everyone, even them. One day the doors will open and we will be rejoined. Until then we wait and we try to improve what we have been given."[PARAGRAPH:1]After that I sat at the feet of his throne, played with Abagail and paid less and less attention to the occurrences of the mortal world. They usually wouldn't even get to Cassiel himself unless the person was someone politically important.[PARAGRAPH:1]"You will stay in the palace tonight. Tomorrow you will awake a new man, put your old life behind you and start a new one here. Your name will be Goodreau. [TAB]He was lost. The realization suddenly dawned on him, in all its cold and inescapable horror. He had no idea where the camp was. Their thick grey fur providing shelter from the wind and ice. Their powerful jaws, with teeth fit for crushing and grinding.[PARAGRAPH:1]For the next few weeks, he followed the wolves. Always taking care to keep a safe distance, he diligently observed the behavior of the pack with a child's curiosity.[PARAGRAPH:1]One thing he noticed was the sheer brutal efficiency that signified its progress, not constrained by the human emotions of compassion and mercy. When the hunt was on, and a prey was taken down, the wolves did not share the spoils equally, but fought to the death for it, young as well as old, male as well as female.[PARAGRAPH:1]At first these things horrified the young Charadon, but gradually the horror gave way to admiration. Because the wolves, thanks to these measures, were very efficient at what they did. By rooting out the weaknesses of individuals, the pack managed to survive. In a world as harsh as this, unyielding cruelty was the greatest tool in the struggle for resources.[PARAGRAPH:1]One day, as he climbed a hillside to get a view of the progress of the pack, he spied the smoke of campfires in the horizon. Greatly uplifted by the sight, he made his way towards the camp. As he approached the camp, moving slowly down the hillside, he gazed at its inhabitants. What a contrast compared to the wolves! Here, the elderly were brought food by the hunters, the children nursed in their mothers' tender embrace and the sick cared for by herbal medicine and gentle treatment. They were glorifying weakness. At this sight, and this realization, something deep in the heart of Charadon went cold and dark. With a clarity both liberating and dreadful, he suddenly knew what he had to do.[PARAGRAPH:1]Charadon stood on the hillside and watched the slaughter. His people had been taken completely by surprise by the pack of wolves. His face was expressionless as he watched them drag his mother out of her tent, and fight over her entrails. His father attempted to stop them, only to be ripped apart by the leader of the pack. As he stood there, silently waiting, what was left of his people, the strongest and fiercest among them, finally managed to drive the wolves away. The worthy ones. He made his way down the hillside, to join up with the survivors. There would be a place for them in the future after all.

[TAB]He fiddled with the pieces of clockwork mechanism, shuffling them around the tabletop, lifting a cogwheel and mounting it on a pin, then giving it a little tip to make it spin. [TAB]Garrim looked at the crystal that lay on the table before him. It had been brought in by the miners yesterday; at first mistaking it for silver, they had lost two of their number to its power. It had yet to be explained why. According to the disturbing tales of the other miners, the workers had simply died when they touched the substance, without it inflicting any visible wound on them. They'd merely fallen to the ground without a sound, their lifeforce disappearing completely. Finally, the miners realized the source of the threat, and one of them, unusually courageous, attempted to pick up the crystal with a piece of cloth, and so it was that they had brought it to him.[PARAGRAPH:1]He was about invoke a basic spell of scrying when his apprentice, Haeris, walked into his study.[PARAGRAPH:1]"What have I told you about knocking?!" Garrim yelled, with a fury more motivated by his tension than by actual irritation. Haeris seemed quite startled at his master's unusual display of temper.[PARAGRAPH:1]"Sorry master, but you'd just sent for me, I thought..." he trailed off.[PARAGRAPH:1]"Hmpf...well, now that you've come, you might as well stay. Who knows, you might even learn something from this. But please be quiet!"[PARAGRAPH:1]Haeris walked closer to the table in silence, but he appeared a bit sullen.[PARAGRAPH:1]Garrim ignored him, and returned his attention to the crystal. It was quite beautiful, and he fully understood why the unlucky miners had felt compelled to pick it up. Lights sparkled within its surface, red, purple and blue. Perhaps it would have been wiser to dispose of it, to take it to one of the deep mineshafts that were scheduled for closing soon, but Garrim had always been very curious about magical artifacts, whether they were benevolent or harmful.[PARAGRAPH:1]He raised his left hand, and started to invoke the spell of scrying. Surprisingly, there was no reaction whatsoever from the substance, he might as well have used the spell on a common rock. Puzzled, he looked closely at the crystal. It still sparkled with light...but it seemed the colors had grown darker while the light grew more intense...a truly unusual phenomenon to behold. As he watched, a dark mist suddenly started to emanate from the crystal, making a hissing sound somewhat akin to that of sulfuric acid liquefying metal. The mist started to approach Garrim, and soon it had surrounded him completely. The hissing sound became louder, and he realized it was actually a chorus of whispers: "You....binder of spells.....we need you...you need us...power...power beyond imagination....follow us...follow us...touch the relic...and you shall be free at last..."[PARAGRAPH:1]Garrim felt himself drawn towards the crystal, and he was about to reach out and touch it when he suddenly pulled himself back through a sheer effort of will. His ears away from the whispers and his head clear once more, he suddenly realized what he was dealing with here. "Mammon..." he muttered under his breath. He leapt backwards as the mist approached again, made a complicated hand-gesture and invoked the most powerful defensive spell he could remember. A pillar of brilliant light appeared before him, and the mist moved backwards, the whispers now more furious than compelling. Garrim drew a breath of relief. That had been close.[PARAGRAPH:1]Relief quickly gave way to terror, as Garrim suddenly saw Haeris on the other side of the barrier, and the mist that was rapidly closing in on him. It enveloped Haeris in much the same way as it had enveloped him moments earlier, but Haeris proved less resilient. He leaned forward and touched the crystal while Garrim watched, stunned by the sheer horror of the events taking place behind the wall of light.[PARAGRAPH:1]Haeris let out a scream of anguish, as a shaft of light from the crystal struck him in the chest. It lingered on as a pulsating beam seemed to be sucking the life away from him. Haeris' face became increasingly distorted, his flesh was slowly drained of all color, and his eyes gained a bluish hue. But suddenly the shaft of dark-red light subsided, and the mist dispersed with it. Garrim regained his senses, quickly dispelled the wall of light, and rushed to the side of his apprentice, who stood with a blank stare in his eyes.[PARAGRAPH:1]"Are you all right? Haeris, speak to me!"[PARAGRAPH:1]At first he merely stared blankly at the crystal in front of him. Then he eyed Garrim, and his pale face was distorted by a sudden sneer.[PARAGRAPH:1]"I am perfectly fine, master... I can see clearly now..."Garrim was shocked to hear the contempt in the voice of his previously amiable apprentice. What came next would prove even more horrifying, however.[PARAGRAPH:2]The battle had been rough. Garrim doubled over and coughed up blood, but managed to stay on his feet. Before him lay the burnt and disfigured corpse of his apprentice and friend, burned-and this was what hurt the most-by Garrim's own spells. Yet he had had no choice. The crystal still laid on the table, its surface now deceptively calm. The idea of throwing it into a deep mineshaft seemed much more compelling now. That thing had never been meant for daylight.

[TAB]Dreamers, worthless vagrants whose only use was receiving the visions of the Overlords, surrounded the chamber. Each lay in a shallow recess, and 27 thin bone needles pierced them in different places. The needles were hollow and filled with wax from whale fat and unholy religious oils, while in each a wick burned. As the wax melted, it seeped down the needle into the dreamers' blood, this was what induced the visions.[PARAGRAPH:1]Most of what they said was gibberish, nightmares and twisted memories. They repeated verses to old lullabies, held conversations with imaginary people, and talked in languages no one could recognize. But occasionally it was more than that.[PARAGRAPH:1]These dreams were always preceded by the Dreamers screaming. New Zealots always considered opening themselves up to receive the dreams directly, to speak directly with the Overlords, until they heard the screams.[PARAGRAPH:1]Then the voice came, a variety of voices but never that of the Dreamer. The message was given, the Cultists would faithfully record it and worship at the sides of the recess. The Dreamer was always mentally scarred by the contact, most were only good for 2 or 3 visions before they were replaced.[PARAGRAPH:1]But there were rules to dealing with the dreamers, they were sacred objects. Their food was specially prepared, they were kept clean and groomed and they weren't exposed to any sound or sight that could distress them, until Cinnia.[PARAGRAPH:1]Cinnia was a favored dreamer of the Overlords, having received 7 visions and all the Cultists except Koun of the Ninth Ring agreed she was fit to receive more. Her 8th vision was her last, the Overlords spoke through her in three voices. One yelled in outrage threatening a great wave would destroy the city if atonement was not met. Another spoke of the future, of a human terror that would lead and destroy men, the "Kraken of Fields". The last voice screamed in pain, it was broken and the Cultists were never able to decipher its message, for it was cut off halfway through the messages of the other two.[PARAGRAPH:1]For weeks the Cultists debated the meanings of the visions. Koun argued that Cinnia should be killed, that her sacrifice was the atonement the Overlords demanded. Each day they watched the sea, fearful of a coming wave. Then the Cultists noticed that the sea was beginning to recede, to pull away from the city. The water was gathering somewhere distant, the wave was coming.[PARAGRAPH:1]They rushed to the chamber, worshipped beside Cinnia, asked for guidance on how to appease their masters. They stayed there until one of them noticed Cinnia's stomach had expanded slightly. A sorcerer confirmed it, she was pregnant.[PARAGRAPH:1]The rest of the day was chaos. A dreamer had been befouled, and only Cultists had access to them. Under threat and coercion they found who had done it: Koun of the Ninth Ring.[PARAGRAPH:1]Koun was sacrificed at the beach and the wave never came. Cinnia was taken from the chamber and tended to. She died in childbirth, but gave birth two girls, one was stillborn, the other survived.[PARAGRAPH:1]The Cultists decided that the child was too dangerous to be kept in the temple, so she was given to a Lanun ship captain to raise. He named her Hannah the Irin, after being told she was a twin whose mother and sister died in childbirth.[PARAGRAPH:1]Hannah became as temperamental and powerful as the sea itself. She left her fathers ship at 15 and led a mutiny against her next ship's captain to take it from him. That ship, which she renamed the 'Desecrated Vessel' became feared by military and merchant ships alike. When the time for war came, pirates flocked to her flag. Unaccustomed to central rule, the Lanun follow Hannah, too afraid to do otherwise.
