Description: Decius takes his battle to the Sidar.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Requires: Successful completion of the Wages of Sin scenario.

After the third group of hunters went missing, Decius started to get upset. The trip south from the lands that he had conquered around Tempus Mor was rife with danger, as mountain passes ended in steep drops as often as not, and even the gentle slopes led down into mist-filled valleys with treacherous bogs and swamplands. They were easy prey at night; even the Nightwatch would often be found slain in the morning. He began to wish that his whole group had taken the sea route again, but he hadn't wanted to risk Overcouncil or Sidar forces coming in from the north and pinching them against the main Sidar army.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Even the Svartalfar hunters who guided them, experts at avoiding detection, would find some among their numbers poached.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Then one morning they awoke to find a whole company of bloodpets dead. Decius ground his teeth as the bit of sun that came through the thick clouds illuminated the grisly scene.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"Commander, may we speak?" The voice came from above as the speaker slowly descended. A succubus, sent with word of Os-Gabella's offer and to assist Decius. It was less an offer and more a plea; were he to return with the blade that slew Ethne of the Elohim, he could name his price from the old sorceress. It was too tempting of an offer for him to pass up, not to mention the value he would get from using these Sidar as his personal spies should he subdue them. But just finding them was proving a most difficult quest.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"Yes, what is it?" Decius averted his eyes from her shapely, and nude, form, not out of modesty but because he didn't want to be reminded at the moment of another woman whose company he had recently kept, the druid Talia Gosam.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"You are a wise commander, but you are still blind to some of the options that are open to you. Why do you grieve the loss of these troops?"[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"I'm not in the mood for games, creature. What is your suggestion?"[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"They did not serve you willingly in life; why let them take to death against your wishes? We can animate these bodies, and send them ahead. Let the Sidar ghosts strike with their poisoned blades against hearts no longer beating."[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"Yes, we'll make them strike twice for every kill."[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"Furthermore, their assassins have been aiming for our scouts and workers, or other weaker troops. Let us petition Esus to deceive their eyes. For Agares to grant us allies more at home in the darkness than our foes are. To Aeron, for strength to fight frenzied even when poisoned and dying. And most importantly, to Ceridwen, for the secret knowledge the great seer holds."[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"I don't like seeking the help of gods. They usually take more than they give."[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"Our gods will not collect on their debt for some time Decius. Their goals align with yours, and they do not seek to pull your strings, as you already follow their path. Their price is cheaper than losing your head to an assassin's blade."[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Decius stared at the demon for a moment. "Very well. What is needed?"[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]The ritual was prepared. Decius's blood was spilled into the fires, and he recited the prayers. In the dancing flames, the valley was illuminated, showing the path to take to the enemy's gates."

The Elohim sent a guide to lead the Malakim to the Astur wastes, and the Ljosalfar lent a skilled elven tracker. The assassin Decius captured was bound and marched at the head of the column.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Still the winding paths claimed many as they traveled in pursuit of the hidden civilization of the Sidar. Mountain passes dropped into valleys cloaked in fog, filled with swamps and ruins. Even when not on the move, men disappeared at night, until a full score of Lightbringers were posted guard each sundown. Even so, the Sidar captive was taken back by his allies one night, out from under the Malakim guards. The next day Decius marched the Malakim forces harder, keeping scouting parties roving constantly around the main force but never out of sight of one another. And still nearly a third of his forces were cut off navigating a swampy valley in the dense fog, lost from the rest of the company. When Decius found out, he ordered his army to stop and set up camp at the nearest hilltop, deciding that it was time to try something new.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"Greetings, lord," the Vicar said as Decius entered the tent used as temple. "Have you orders?"[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"No. I would like to pray." The Vicar nodded, lighting incense and beginning the recitation of Lugus's noontime prayer.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"I meant alone." Decius waited while the Vicar left. Decius stood, then knelt, then finally sat near the altar, arms crossed and staring into the brazier.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]This was a holy place, but Decius felt no special kinship to Lugus, despite his friend's devotion. Junil and  justice he had been taught to revere, but Decius had betrayed Junil's chosen people. Who should he turn to? Sirona, Ethne's patron? Sucellus, God of Life? Or... who? His theological knowledge didn't extend very deep, and shortly gave up trying to decide the best recipient of his pleas.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"Oh gods who love justice and oppose the spreading darkness, hear me. I have failed you in the past, sometimes greatly. I have been rash and selfish, and am not a disciple of your ways. But you have failed me as well, or least your followers and laws have. Do not let my people die in this valley of death. A good woman's soul is doomed if we fail. And if the Calabim and their allies manage to subdue these Sidar ghosts, they stand to turn the tide of the war we've almost won. Surely the end of the world should draw your attention? Surely opposing this grave evil merits your favor? I am an imperfect champion, but do not let these good people suffer for my impurity. Show me the way, and I yield my will to you."[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Decius waited briefly for a sign. Then sighed and left the tent.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]The fog had lifted from the valley, and the clouds above had parted. The way was made clear. Hunters' hawks took flight. Soon they learned that they were not far from the enemy's borders, and the treacherous passage would be safer in this clear day.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"Should we continue the march?" asked one of his commanders.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"Not yet. Set up a permanent encampment here. This hill is the place of our deliverance, from where we will prepare to take the Sidar capital and their warriors as our vassals."

This is but a room, the voice said, "And your entrance here means nothing. We will leave this place and find another."[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"This isn't the first of your cities that have been conquered, shade. I will not give up until you yield. The world is not as big as it once was, when it emerged from winter wild and open. Places to hide are running out."[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Sandalphon appeared behind him. "What do you want, Decius? A Sidar assassin to strike against your father in Torrolerial? He has his hands full with the Doviello invasion, I think. We could slay Varn Gosam in his sleep, if you still despise him, or free you from your obligations to Flauros while he feeds."[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"You know so much about me? I think it is time for you to start answering my questions."[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"Giving answers isn't what we do. We watch and plan and wait and, if absolutely necessary, we act, without the world knowing we were here. To preserve the Sidar and our seclusion." Sandalphon faded from view again. Decius turned to Losha Valus, and gestured to the slain shades scattered around the Sidar throne room. Losha and the other vampires accompanying Decius raised them as skeletons.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"Face me Sandalphon, or every Sidar man, woman, and child we have killed or will ever find will be raised as a skeleton and sent to hunt you down. Will you enjoy your long life being forever invisible?"[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"No!" Sandalphon's rage was the first emotion he had shown. "Leave them be. You have no right to abuse the dead. These bodies are all that remains in this world of our friends, and you have no right to enslave them. I will yield to you."[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Decius nodded, and Losha released the bodies of the slain shades. "I want to know why you attacked me."[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"The Calabim are an intriguing people, not unlike us until recently. You have led them to be more aggressive with your leadership, since you did not face the hardship that they saw during the Age of Winter. After your success in the war of Tempus Mor, we predicted a resurgent Calabim ruling over the entire world, and feasting on the Sidar. The risk of this outweighed the risk of revealing ourselves, and so we activated our assassins in the area. Unfortunately, only Rathus accomplished his goal."[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"He was the one who struck at the Elohim, then? I have a friend who badly wants his sword." Decius pulled out the Nether Blade that they had taken from Rathus's corpse and examined it. Green runes pulsed along the light ebon blade. "What makes this sword special?"[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"The Nether Blade is an artifact from the underworld. Its power draws any it slays into Arawns lands and anchors them in his vault."[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"Hmm. I think this might be better than whatever Os-Gabella could offer me. It isn't enough to compensate us for all that we have lost since your attack on us... but I dare not invite you into our midst; it would only be inviting my death. We will take what we need of your supplies and leave you here in peace, to live your long, quiet, isolated lives. But the secrets of the Sidar will be spread far and wide among the Calabim. If you strike at us again, everything that you have built will be destroyed and your people will be put to death and then enslaved until the end of time."[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"This is as generous as we can expect from you, I am well aware," Sandalphon replied. Suddenly from behind him another ghost appeared, drawing their attention. "Belthus, welcome back," Sandalphon said. "How went your mission?"[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"Auric Ulvin's war will not be stopped so easy. I could not get near him. He radiates with the power of Winter, a power not seen on Erebus for generations, and his army grows more numerous. It seems the endless winter is more likely than we thought."[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"Who is this Auric Ulvin?"[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"Belthus, this is Decius of the Calabim. We were just discussing the future sovereignty of the Sidar in light of the Calabim's brutal conquest. Decius, we have our eye on more than just the nations nearest us. In the distant Aquillo Tundra occur events that could trouble us even here. Auric is a magical prodigy, and this power made him a suitable vessel for the machinations of the power of winter. Mulcarn was killed by the Godslayer, leaving his sphere without a suitable ruler. Auric has drawn together the tools of that god, and is preparing to become its avatar. Belthus was sent to stop him, but we acted too late. If the armies gathering against him do not stop him, he will return all Erebus to an Age of Winter."[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Decius looked at the sword he held in his hands for a moment, then he sheathed it. "What if a god was not slain with the Godslayer, but trapped by the Nether Blade?"[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Sandalphon shrugged. "We have no experience with that."[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"Auric poses a grave threat. We will go to support those who stand against him, and if the Nether Blade staves off this threat for good, perhaps it can rid me of my troublesome allies as well."

This is but a room, the voice said, "And your entrance here means nothing. We will leave this place and find another."[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"This isn't the first of your cities that have been conquered, shade. I will not give up until you yield. The world is not as big as it once was, when it emerged from winter wild and open. Places to hide are running out."[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Sandalphon appeared behind him. "What do you want, Decius? A Sidar assassin to strike against your father in Torrolerial? He has his hands full with the Doviello invasion, I think. Would you prefer we poison the Calabim lords? We prefer not to draw the attention of other immortals to ourselves; we are still new at this and they may know more than us."[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"You know so much about me, do you? I think it is time for you to start answering my questions."[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"Giving answers isn't what we do. We watch and plan and wait and, if absolutely necessary, we act, without the world knowing we were here. To preserve the Sidar and our seclusion." Sandalphon faded from view again. Decius turned to Vaughn, and the Paladin brought forth a relic of Lugus, flooding the room with light, revealing Sandalphon sitting calmly on his throne. "You seem to have me at a disadvantage. What are your terms?"[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"I want to know why you attacked Ethne and me."[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"You were both instrumental in leading the war in Tempus Mor, dangerously close to this secluded valley. And you were winning. Based on our observations of your actions in the desert of Myrh, we calculated that an empowered Overcouncil flush with victory would try to expand its position here, attempting to bring us under their 'enlightened' sovereignty. The risk of inaction seemed greater than the risk of action, so we activated our assassins in the region, to attempt to bring a stalemate to the battle and dissuade you from going further. Unfortunately, our plans failed, and here you are."[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"This is what you do? You decide who lives and dies based on what you think that they will do?"[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Sandalphon sneered at Decius, the first hint of emotion that he displayed. "You are so much better? You are a ruler-you decide who lives and dies among the untold number that dwell within your borders. Among your soldiers you execute those who betray or desert you, and unleash them on those who would stand against you. You exercise the power of the judge over many, yet you take offense at we who dare to judge only a few, only the kings or priests or generals?"[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"You have no authority over me."[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"We have the same authority over you that you have over your citizens-we have the power to act on our judgments."[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Decius sighed. "I had come hoping to take you as my vassal, to use you against my enemies. I see now that that would be a foolish plan, only inviting my death or that of my heir. Here is what I propose instead. Give me an advisor. We will leave you to yourselves, to live your long, quiet, isolated lives, but send one of your number to sit in our councils, not as a member but to warn us before you strike. Why should my death be your first course of action?"[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Sandalphon considered him. "This is acceptable. Provided that you personally tell no one of our existence. You can work through your council to see that our few interests are maintained, and we shall likewise leave the world alone for as long as we think wise."[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"There is one other condition. I want the soul of Ethne freed. She was slain and cannot be resurrected."[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"The Elohim woman... Rathus took the Nether Blade when he attacked her, because she knows the secrets of the Mercurian Gate, passed down through the regents of the Elohim."[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"There is no point it slaying her for that now; the secret has been used, and spread throughout the Empyrean to Bourne the Gleaming. Release her spirit."[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"The Nether Blade is an artifact from the underworld. It will draw the soul of anyone it slays into Arawns realm and anchors them there. Destroying it should free those whose souls belong elsewhere. Free them to serve their true lord, be it in their vault or recalled to Erebus."[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"Then I shall do so, and free Ethne to return to her people." Decius pulled out the blade that they had taken from Rathus's corpse and studied it for a moment. Green runes pulsed along the light ebon blade.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Behind Sandalphon another Ghost appeared suddenly, drawing their attention. "Belthus, welcome back," Sandalphon said. I know that name..." said Decius.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"Who is this?" asked Belthus.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"Decius leads the Malakim army. They have discovered us, but we have come to an understanding."[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"Varn Gosam met Auric Ulvin. Varn gave up his vaunted position among a secluded elven tribe to free him, though it would have cost them both their lives had Auric's great power not manifested."[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"Auric is a magical prodigy, and this power made him a suitable vessel for the machinations of the power of winter. Mulcarn was killed by the Godslayer, leaving his sphere without a suitable ruler. Auric has drawn together the tools of that god, and is preparing to become its avatar. Belthus was sent to stop him, but we acted too late. If the armies gathering against him do not stop him, he will return all Erebus to an Age of Winter."[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Decius looked at the sword he held in his hands for a moment, then he sheathed it. "What if a god was not slain with the Godslayer, but trapped by the Nether Blade?"[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Sandalphon shrugged. "We have no experience with that. I thought you intended to free your friend?"[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"Auric poses a grave threat. We will go to support those who stand against him, and if the Nether Blade staves off this threat for good... I can only hope that Ethne forgives me."

Where you die I will die, and there I will be buried. May the Lord deal with me, be it ever so severely, if anything but death separates you and me.-ancient Umberguard intonement[NEWLINE][NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Dwarves bent down and clutched the ground. They squeezed until their knuckles turned white from the strain and almost crawled across the mountainside refusing to let go with both hands at once. One group sat huddled beneath a rocky outcropping, as if trying to evade a storm, though the day was sunny and beautiful.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Palais Adien stood just outside the tunnel entrance and stared into the sky. He slowly began to sway, then collapsed and vomited all over the ground. His brothers rushed to him, all careful not to look up.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Arturus watched his kin struggle. A wild hare stopped briefly to look at the odd dwarves before hopping away. The dwarves were as equally confused by the bouncing rabbit as it was by the slinking dwarves.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"Look out across the plains," Arturus shouted and then he waited for all the dwarves to do as he commanded. From here he could see the green and browns of distant hills, the blues of inland lakes and the rich yellows of fertile valleys. Once the dwarves were all looking Arturus continued.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"The mountain does not move. Even as the wind strikes it, as storms rage against it the mountain does not move. With the open sky above and the underhome below, as ages pass, as empires and gods battle the mountain does not move."[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]At this point Arturus was standing in the open. He could see the fear in his clansmen's eyes as they looked at him. With only his feet touching the earth, as if he would be sucked off into the unknown. But he remained solid and determined.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"We will be as the mountain. We will build the first Khazad surface cities here since the Age of Magic. And though we may face the dangers of this world, though creatures or the empires of men may attack we, like the mountain, will not move."[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]One by one the dwarves stood then together they walked down the mountainside toward the site of their first city.

The men were simply gone. Arturus didn't know if their gold ran out or if they simply tired of the war. Such are the ways of men that the passions of one day are forgotten tomorrow.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Regardless, the tide of onrushing horsemen had stopped and the Khazad were firmly entrenched upon the surface of Erebus.
These jungles are not as easily tamed as the Umbrawood. This is no place for elves, or men.
Even mighty stones wear to the steady pressure of rivers and tides. So are we before the unending hordes of the Clan.
The taint of Labruscum will endure. There must be some small part of Bannor strength left within these beasts.
I will not bear the yoke of Sheelba any longer. You can have this poisoned jungle, there is better hunting elsewhere.
We are best to surrender the Labruscum entirely to the canticle of fire. I would do so, but the Clan may be crazed enough to enjoy it.
I pray that you follow me out of this jungle before it is too late. I have no desire to see another barrow raised in this land, or to find you buried beneath it.
A thousand will come after me. We will defeat you with our strength our drown you in our blood. There is no victory to be found here.
I am not being paid nearly enough for this war. I leave you to your convictions, I will seek my glory elsewhere.

Description: Labruscum has long been the home of the Clan of Embers. If they can be removed here their grip on Erebus will be weakened.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Special Rules: The lowest ranked player will be removed every 50 turns until only 5 players remain. This does not apply to the Clan of Embers players.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Reward: Completing this scenario reduces the amount of Barbarians in all other scenarios.

The jungles of Labruscum cover what once was the heart of the Bannor empire. The fall of the Queen of Fire reduced that nation to ash and transformed her followers into a savage mix of orcs, goblins and other savage humanoids. Now Labruscum serves as the recruiting ground for the Clan of Embers, and if the Clan is to be stopped they must be defeated here.

Labruscum is under your control. Without their wildlands the Clan's grip on Erebus is weakened and your homeland will be spared the worst of their raids. Civilization will rise again from the jungle ruins.
I should have known better than to trust mercenaries for my defense. You are too weak to serve a god.
We stood alone against the Illians at the end of the Age of Magic. We will rise up again.
Is the hope of man so easily lost? Given away for a few gold and sold to simple bandits. Is this how we will lose this age?
My golems would have crushed you, if you would only stand still...
Each man eventually becomes food for another, today my legacy is ended.
You are a puppet for the White Hand, they will sacrifice you when it serves their needs.

Description: Regain the Pieces of Barnaxus for Auric Ulvin.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Special Rules: You cannot train units, instead they must be purchased. Auric pays you a bounty for every enemy unit you defeat. [NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Requires: Successful completion of the Blood of Angels scenario.
Capture the Pieces of Barnaxus and take them to the Illian capital

Thick curls of smoke floated up from the camp's remains. Whatever army had camped there was gone now.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"It's like chasing the wind," Lucian said in frustration, "what is the point of a mercenary army if you can never catch up with them long enough to hire them?"[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"Is it possible they were defeated here; I heard they were involved in the war between the sandmen and the cabal."[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Auric considered Riuros's suggestion, "Maybe. There must be survivors from one side or the other, send out the scouts and see if they can track some down. I want to talk to any Hippus they find, so make sure they aren't attacked."[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]That last instruction was for Lucian; the Doviello scouts were excellent trackers but horrible diplomats.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE][NEWLINE]A few days later they had three different reports from the scouts. One reported Hippus commanders in the Calabim city of Acaia gloating of their victory and the wisdom hiring them. Another reported disheveled Hippus units in the Malakim city of Bryn that spoke of a crushing loss on the plains. The last reported a significant Hippus army massed in a nearby valley, looking unbloodied and well rested.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]But when they arrived at the valley the Hippus were gone, as were any signs that they had been there. The scout stared dumbfounded at the empty valley and would have been beaten for leading the army to the empty valley if Riuros didn't spot a small band of riders under the Hippus flag heading toward them.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]There were four riders. Tasunke was as close as the Hippus had to a king, and his three captains let him do the talking. After introductions Tasunke asked if Auric wanted to hire the Hippus.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"Yes," Auric answered, "the capture of Torrolerial and Midgar has deepened our treasury but shortened our time. I want to hire you to go to the Finnian Fields and recover an item from the Luchuirp, a golem named Barnaxus."[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"How are we to know which golem is the right one? Battle doesn't often allow for the exchange of pleasantries."[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Auric paused, then to the surprise of Lucian and the priests he ignored Tasunke's sarcasm and returned only a thin, insincere smile.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"Barnaxus has the mark of the white hand upon him. Find the golem with that mark and bring him to me to earn your reward."[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"That we can do." Tasunke replied, "But I will need money to finance the move of my army to the Finnian Fields. The Luchuirp aren't likely to give up their golem so easily."[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Auric thought carefully before responding.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"I will pay for every enemy you kill upon the fields. Show dedication to your task and you will be able to bring your men. Relax in valley camps and pretend to fight wars and you will get no money from me."[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"I am agreed. We will see you on the fields." And with that Tasunke and his captains were off.

Sorry he couldn't be brought back in better shape, he put up a fight.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Auric ignored Tasunke's comment. He was staring reverently at the broken pieces of Barnaxus that Tasunke had laid on the meeting rooms sturdy table. Auric touched each piece carefully, as if they were religious artifacts.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Lucian stood near the door of the chamber, seeming the least confused by Auric's actions but only because he had given up trying to understand them. Dumannios, Riuros, and Anagantios all watched Auric carefully, sensing something deeply significant in the golem's shattered parts but unable to tell what. Tasunke just waited to get paid.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]The room's only other occupant was caged. Beeri Bawl, Luchuirp king, sat ignobly in an old wolf pen that Tasunke had dragged along as a special present for Auric. Beeri was the most surprised to find that Barnaxus was not only the cause of the war with the Hippus, but of so much interest to the Illian priests.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"This is not a golem," Auric began, "he is not powered by gears and dwarven enchantment but by the divine breath of Mulcarn himself. This is the last piece of Mulcarn, that which was untouched by the Godslayer."[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"Oh yeah, that golem's a god. I got a pair of boots made out of Bhall's panties too if you're interested. They smell kinda funny but sure do keep your toes warm on a cold night."[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Everyone but Auric glowered at Beeri, but he only crossed his arms and stared back at them.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Auric placed his hands on the chest of the broken golem and began chanting. The spell started low and quiet as he repeated each incantation. To Tasunke it sounded like a lullaby, but in a language he had never heard. It wasn't harsh or chaotic like the spells he was used to hearing.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]As Auric continued to cast the room chilled to the point where everyone's breath could be seen. Outside of Auric's spell the rest of the sound dimmed and Beeri yelled and thrashed against the bars of his cage, but it went unnoticed.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Barnaxus's chest began to glow. As everyone watched a white radiance spread along the broken pieces and then gathered in his chest before flaring in the symbol of a white hand. The flare was so bright everyone was momentarily blinded, but when they could see again the shadow of Mulcarn stood above the table.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Dumannios, Riuros, and Anagantios fell to their knees. Tasunke felt his knees wobble, as if subconsciously wanting to worship the figure before him, but he resisted.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Mulcarn wasn't there, he wasn't real. It was only a glimmer of his power like the glow of sunlight after it has passed beneath the mountains. But still there was godhood in that image. And in that moment, with Auric standing arms outstretched before the last remnant of Mulcarn's power he did look like a man ascending to heaven.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]The light turned to pale mist and Auric breathed it in. His body strained against the energy that coursed through it, then faded leaving him triumphant and weary for the experience. The three priests continued praying, but did so now at Auric's feet.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Looking at Lucian Auric said, "See that the horse lord is paid well for his service."[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Tasunke smiled, "and what of the dwarf I brought you?"[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Auric considered Beeri closely, "He's very funny. Sell him to Perpentach, I'm sure the Momus can use another jester."
If a man is killed in his sleep, he is not to blame, but the faithless cur that slept at his feet.
I know too well the drive of madness, and I know where it will take you. There are worse things than lost battles and burnt cities.
This will not be the age of the Doviello, such days are past.
Without the threat of hell the Bannor have grown weak. Capria will return from the Fane reforged. The Bannor can withstand any army if their faith is maintained.

Description: Auric needs divine blood to start his rituals. Lead him in his campaign against the Bannor.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Special Rules: Declarations of war are controlled by the scenario.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Requires: Successful completion of the Return of Winter scenario.
Capture the Bannor city of Torrolerial
Capture the Grigori city of Midgar

Auric spent days within his tent as the army waited. He wasn't planning or meeting with his captains, but possessed of a deep depression and sleeping. No one was able to rouse him from his tent and those that tried were met either with anger or simply ignored. The aenemic Illian warriors feared upcoming battles and the Doviello complained that there wasn't battle enough.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Until the morning Auric walked out and viewed the milling troops. He was once again a god king and at his command the army rose up and was ready to march. He spoke of their upcoming victories, of the returning God of Winter, blood enough to satiate the savage Doviello and the glory of a world once again under the hand of the Illians. And the army cheered.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]This was his way, battling between inhuman passion and despair. Both emotions overwhelmed and drove him on.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"Only the immortals can funnel the divine, if I mean to ascend it will be through their blood."[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Lucian followed behind Auric and his captains. The captains asked questions, and Auric answered cryptically or not at all, they advised against direct attack on the civilized lands and Auric was disgusted with them. He finally turned at looked at the trailing Lucian.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"What of the Doviello, have you the courage to reclaim your place beside winter's throne?"[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"My men are ready," Lucian answered, "how would you like them deployed?"[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Auric smiled. "Your faith will be rewarded. We will attack into the Bannor lands, we will assault their capital and march into their largest cathedral. Within there is a holy chamber where loyal Sabathiel rests. We will enter and pull the archangel from the chamber, and then sacrifice him on the cathedral floor to power our ritual."[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]The Illian captains' white skin paled even further; they were shocked beyond speech.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Lucian replied, "When you command it, the Doviello will be ready."[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Auric nodded and Lucian returned to his men. They grumbled at the wasted days and he promised they would have ample opportunity to fight ahead. Lucian kept his concerns to himself.

Lucian loosed his men to ravage Torrolerial. The battle had been hard fought and they had earned their reward. He followed Auric into the cathedral flanked by Illian captains who cut down the remaining priests defending the building.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]The walls were covered in scenes of the Bannor's battles in hell. In each Sabathiel or Capria stood protectively over the loyal soldiers. In one a single Bannor soldier stood before a closing portal with a host of demons around him.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]At the center of cathedral was a chamber covered with the symbols of Junil. A door set with a blazing sword was the only way into the chamber and the laws to enter were inscribed on it. It claimed that the area beyond was between this world and heaven, that it was sanctified ground and that only the high priests could open or pass through the door.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Auric ignored the warnings and threw the door open. Lucian readied his axe; he didnt know what to expect from an archangel but his axe hadn't failed him yet.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]But the chamber beyond was empty. There was only dust inside, no one had entered the chamber for years.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"Has Sabathiel fled?" one of the captains asked.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"No." Despite his frustration Auric smiled. "The priests have been lying to the people. They claim that their laws are passed down from the archangel that protected them in hell but he abandoned them long ago. But they continue to use his legend to control the Bannor. This lie has cost them their capital."[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"And what of our ritual?"[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"It seems we have another debt to repay. Sabathiel is not the only archangel in Erebus-there is one within the Grigori lands as well."

Midgar burned. The Grigori capital was a stark contrast to that of the Bannor. Where the Bannor had temples the Grigori have meeting halls. Where the Bannor had religious symbols the Grigori had graceful art. Most noticeably the architecture of Alexandria shared a common design of fortified buildings, flags and banners. The Grigori buildings were as dissimilar as the people who made them.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]But the tapestry of buildings was united by the palace at its center. There was nothing like it in the city and its beautiful black and copper parapets were a source of inspiration for all the citizens. A testament to what men could create. When he wasn't in his throne room Cassiel himself spent hours within the palace's towers, looking out over his city.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]No doubt Cassiel knew we were coming. Many had fled from the city before Auric's army arrived. Lucian assumed the palace would be as empty as Sabathiel's chamber within the cathedral. Auric was becoming more despondent as they marched toward the capital, and in the past few days even the news of their victories had gone unnoticed as he was retreating more and more into the grip of depression.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]But this morning he arose again reborn. And everyone scrambled to keep up with him as he marched through the capital toward the palace. Ignoring the orders to flee a few loyal craftsmen defended the palace, their love for their king overruling their fear of the invading armies. Their defense was short lived and Auric marched into the throne room.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Cassiel stood in the center of the chamber. He was tall, and perfectly formed, as if a sculptor had formed the ideal man out of marble. There was no doubt that he was an archangel and in his eyes you could see the wisdom gained in his immortal life, and the weight of its burden upon him.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"I worried that I would need to raze every Grigori city in Erebus before I would find you." Auric said.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"Leave my children be, I am the one you want."[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]With that Auric commanded the Illian captains forward and they bound the archangel with four massive iron manacles brought especially for the purpose. Cassiel's clothes were torn off and a team of men took each chain, two for his arms and two for his legs and pulled them taunt. Lifting Cassiel off the ground and stretching him out until he screamed.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Those screams echoed through the palace halls and out into the city. There was so much torment and pain in them that everyone paused, saddened by their sound. Where Doviello soldiers brutally beat the last of the city's defenders both stopped to listen to the cries. For the first time the Doviello questioned their battle, and the dying Grigori shared tears with their leader.[PARAGRAPH:1]"There is a rescue waiting for you" Auric taunted, "A god who may be willing to accept you back in his ara. Will you trade the ideology of three ages for a chance to retain your immortal soul? Are you willing to admit that you exist only to serve the gods? How do you feel about divine intervention now that it is the only thing that can save you?"[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Cassiel didn't reply except to scream louder as his shoulders were ripped from their sockets with a dull pop. His shoulders flushed deep purple with blood and his arms rotated without restriction, only held to his body by skin and a few remaining tendons.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Auric took out a copper dagger and held it over Cassiel's heart.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"And when you die what heaven will accept you? I suspect only Agares will accept one who has so openly defied the gods."[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"You are a farmer's son," Cassiel replied with great strain, "a boy who loved reading and nature. This voice that drives is not you. It promises power but it will imprison you. You must give up this war or you will ruin many lives, including your own."[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Auric ignored the warning and plunged the dagger into Cassiel's heart. The archangel's scream echoed throughout the capital. The men holding the chains continued pulling in those last few seconds until Cassiel died and then they let his body drop onto the floor.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Everyone except Auric waited to see if Cassiel would be reborn, but he didn't move. Auric was finishing the ritual with the bloodied dagger. Slowly, carefully, he completed the spell by pushing the daggers blade into his right hand, cutting his flesh and allowing his blood to mix with the dead archangel.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]In that moment, in a thousand different places in Erebus prophets received visions of a white dragon swallowing the world. Priests were overcome with a sense of foreboding and a cool wind blew through even the warmest areas. Auric's ascension had begun.
Load this to play any of the Fall from Heaven II scenarios
The commander of Tor Alessi sends his thanks for clearing the barrow. He had some siege equipment commissioned that he no longer needs and he gifts it to your war effort.

Welcome, Decius. We have been expecting you. My name is Confessor Wallon. It is Sabathiel's will that I accompany you. The Diviners' have great fears about the safety of our southwest settlements, indeed, of the whole empire if the threat growing there spreads. We should set out there at once.
A confessor has joined your ranks.

Description: The Bannor Empire is a nation born of tragedy, struggle, and endless war. A people sustained by piety, honor, and unyielding discipline. An uncompromising people gathers many enemies, but the Bannor have no shortage of heroes. Such as Decius, a man brave, loyal, and ever steadfast. But an uncompromising man gains many enemies as well. In the Fall of Cuantine, Decius is called upon to face a threat that grows near the heart of the Empire, in the seemingly peaceful Adian Fields...[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Special Rules: Rosier must survive.
Take your units to the city Brigit's Light Abbey
Defeat the twisted men in the southern jungle and destroy their lair
Research Orders from Heaven to gain Rosier and pillage Muirin's lair
Wait for the twisted men to return to their homes
Raze the Octopus Overlord's holy city

Decius wipes the goblin blood from his sword and without pause begins the next task-razing the fort the goblins were using to launch attacks at the Bannor outpost. He is soon interrupted by a messenger. "Decius Achare, you are requested by the Lady Commanders." Decius nods and sets his men to tearing down the goblin fortifications.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"Decius, I am sending you back to Torrolerial."[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"Yes milady. May I speak freely?"[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"Of course."[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"Why send a man of action back to the capital? This seems a demotion to me."[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Capria smiles. "No, it is not a demotion nor is it my decision. The Diviner claims it is of great importance that you do so, or all of the Empire is imperiled. So go at once and report to your father." Decius turned to gather supplies, and was riding homeward within the hour.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Decius entered the meeting hall of House Achare's stronghold. "I have come, Lord Commander, though I know not why. Lady Capria had good use of me in the front."[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Lord Samatheon replied, "We are off the field, my son, you can drop my title. Your name has gained some renown, and I would grant you your command. Though you are right to suspect that I would leave you to Lady Capria until the completion of her campaign if I could. While the Diviners are as forthcoming as usual, they must be heeded, and they have expressed grave concerns about supernatural threats in this region. Since your brother has taken his command south to reinforce the Labuscrum, I need a commander I can trust for House Achares legions. I place you in command of our expeditionary force; unfortunately you will be need an 'advisor.'"[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"I thank you for your trust, father, I shall do you proud."[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"As the priests say, first to your god, then to your king, then to your commander. Go therefore to the Abbey of Brigit's Light, then to the duties they have for our forces. Return home when you can, for I would like much to hear news of your travels. Dismissed."

Your confessor approaches you as you prepare your army to move. "Commander Decius, we have uncovered the source of the taint we discovered in the jungles. In fact, it stems from the ports of the Lanun. We had negotiated trade relations with the Lanun, but apparently they have allowed their cities to be infested by the Overlords. We must wipe out every city with the Octopus Overlords religion."[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Rosier says "So you only freed the twisted men in order to track them down and destroy them?"[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"If these people have given their souls to demons, their lives are forfeit. If their Oaths hold true, they shall dwell with Junil forever. Either way we shall protect the Bannor from this taint, and the power of the good shall not fade nor flicker from the face of Erebus."[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"This seems less of good than of power to me, Decius." says Rosier.

A Speaker is brought before you as you watch the destruction of the Lanun's Temple of the Overlords. "Your trespass here is unforgivable! This sacred ground rings with echoes of the depths."[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"Your allegiance to evil has sealed your fate," Wallon says.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"Fate is ours to twist, and vengeance mine to take. Rise, servants!"[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Decius scans the horizon, then shouts to his advisors, "Look to the horizon! Drown rise from the depths and head for Cuantine. We cannot get there before them on foot."[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Rosier says "The artifacts of these cultists, I have seen them used to travel over the water."[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"We cannot risk the taint these bear," the Confessor tells him.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"Foolish priest, it is worth the risk. You gamble the lives of our people for your purity's sake? You follow your law, then, and I will follow my own heart." Rosier dons the mask of the Speaker, and heads towards the waves.

There is a lair ahead, a dwelling of barbarians that will menace civilized lands until defeated. But this one is guarded by a Barbarian Hero. Confessor Wallon speaks, "Our forces seem reluctant to fight, despite my exhortations. I bid thee research Orders from Heaven, that we might make use of the Oath-taker Heroes. In fact, I find your tardiness to study the will of Junil disappointing, but that is a matter for another time. Heroes such as Rosier will grow more powerful with time, so you can wait until this battle is to our advantage."
Rosier must survive to complete this scenario.

The Confessor walks among the ruins of the lair. "This is surely the taint Junil has warned us of. We must eliminate the camp and everyone in it."[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Rosier is reluctant to follow his command. "Many of these twisted men were slaves and captives. By what right do we put them to the sword?"[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"The Bannor Empire is the sole beacon of hope for this world. Should we allow taint to spread this close to the heart of the Empire?"[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"We should trust our god enough to let innocent men return to their homes."[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]" ...Perhaps you are right. Very well, Commander Decius, should they give their Oath to Rosier, I will permit them return to their homes. Then we should return to the Abbey."

Description: Dain means to pass the pass the trials of the Cave of Ancestors.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Special Rules: This is a dungeon adventure. You control one unit through the challenges of the scenario and if that unit dies you lose.

During the Age of Magic Kylorin used magical trials to separate common mages from the truly talented. The things that appeared in the trials were illusions, but the risk of death was real. Most died, but the few that passed the trials went on to be some of the most powerful archmages of their age.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Some or the leaders in the current age, such as Os-Gabella and Perpentach, went through these trials when Patria was still the only empire of man. Others, such as Laroth, Barbatos or Trenton Majosi are less well known survivors of the trials.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]It was hundreds of years into the Age of Rebirth before Dain of the Amurites, discovered the records of these magical trials. They were considered archaic, a violent reminder of Patria during its darkest hours. The culture of the Amurites celebrated public study of magic and this was seen as a more enlightened approach.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]But Dain wondered how he compared to the Patrian archmages. And was even more interested in the greater talent the trial seemed to imbue in the lucky few who survived. Dain searched for, and found several locations for these trials, but most were simply empty towers, dungeons or cave labyrinths. Until in the year 441 of the fourth age Dain found the location of one that was still active.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]The locals, a group of Balseraph fishermen living on the edge of their empire, long ago learned to avoid the cave; no one who entered it ever came out. They claimed death himself lived within it. They also claimed that chickens were divine, so Dain didnt take their warnings very seriously.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]With a spellstaff and healing salve ready, as these were the traditional aides given to those taking the trial, Dain entered the cave.
Courage- Makes units immune to Fear. It also slightly improves the units heal rate.

Fireball- Summons a ball of fire which the caster can hurl at enemies from 2 plots away, farther if the caster has extension promotions. Fireball does fire damage to the enemy unit it strikes and some collateral damager to other units in the stack. Note that a lot of creatures, including most demons and orcs have some fire resistance, making this spell less effective against them. But some units, such as the Drown and Wood Golems are vulnerable to fire damage and take additional damage form fireballs.

Floating Eye- Summons a Floating Eye which is unable to attack but useful for exploring dangerous areas without risking your caster. Floating Eyes can also see invisible units so it's a good way to find hidden enemies.
Only someone with arcane talent can open the chest.

Maelstrom- Does lightning damage to all units within 2 tiles. Be careful with it as it doesn't distinguish between enemy, neutral and friendly units and it will be treated as a declaration of war if you damage another players units with it. Maelstrom can't reduce a unit below 50% damage, so its best used to weaken enemy units before sending your warriors in to do battle.

Thank you! the Sidar adept gasps, "I was able to slip by most of the creatures in here but the Hellhounds weren't fooled by my invisibility. Please take this potion, it will allow you to slip by the orcs that guard this maze."[PARAGRAPH:1]After handing you the potion the adept disappears.

Raise Skeleton- Allows you to summon a skeleton to serve you. The skeleton will last until it is killed, but as long as it exists the caster won't be able to summon any more. Skeleton can learn promotions and level up but their low strength keeps them from being that threatening. Also some of their strength comes from Death magic, which isn't used against units like Golems, Demons and other Undead.
Spring- Use spring to transform desert tiles into plains tiles. It can also be used to put out fires in surrounding tiles.

Three years after Dain successfully passed the trial he had a Cave of Ancestors built in Cevedes. Although some still died in the trials the study of the Amurites served them well in preparing mages before they entered. The trial was always open, but never required, for any mages to enter. And some did go through before they were ready to tragic results. But outside of those mistakes it continues to be a legacy of Patria and cornerstone of Amurite tradition.
There is an air rune on the door ahead. As you approach the rune flares up and pushes you back.
There is a fire rune on the door ahead. As you approach the rune flares up and pushes you back.

Bears are powerful predators. Left on their own they will form dens in the wild that produce more bears. Those dens could threaten your explorers, or provide an ample supply of experience for your early warriors.

Although powerful, wild elephants cannot attack, so your units are safe around them. If you capture one and have the Horseback Riding technology you can train captured elephants as war elephants which are able to attack and become powerful early units.
Because of their rarity gorillas are the most difficult animal to capture on most maps. They tend to appear in jungles, though even then you are unlikely to find large groups.
The most prized of animal captures, griffons are not only formidable fighters, but their ability to fly may make them the best early explorers in the game.
Lions are typically found in desert environments. They occasionally can grow into lion prides after kills and lion prides can form dens which spawn new lions.

Giant spiders are invisible to all but recon units. They lay in wait in forested areas and attack units that draw to close to them. Sometimes wild giant spiders or captured ones will produce baby spiders after kills. These can grow to giant spiders after feeding.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Giant spiders are poisonous and will poison units that defeat them in combat. To get rid of this effect have your units healed by a priest or if your unit starts the turn completely healed the poison will wear off.
Tigers are dangerous hunters and very capable of taking out a lone scout or unguarded settler. There is more to fear in the jungles than just the lizardmen.

Wolves can grow to packs after kills and packs can spawn new wolves when they defeat living opponents. This is similar to the den ability of bears and lions but since the wolf pack moves, it is harder for players to farm them for experience.
Description: Capture the animals for Keelyn's Grand Menagerie.
You need %d1 more animals to build the Menagerie
Capture a Bear and cage it in your capital

Falamar... Chaeli whispered.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]He pushed her against one of the massive crates that littered the docks of Dunwich. The moon was well past its zenith and the narrow gap between two crates where they found themselves was hidden in shadows. It was a beautiful night, but the stink of the docks hung thick in the air.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]She leaned back as his kisses wandered down her neck to her very ample bosom. Only stopping when she playfully pulled his hands away when they reached inside her bodice.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"Ain't ya ever wanted to be with the legendary Falamar?" he asked and she smiled radiantly, letting him grope her until he began pulling up on her dress.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"No, no," she said, "just kiss me."[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]There was a second of anger in his eyes, even in her drunken haze Chaeli recognized it, she had seen it before from other men and it never ended well.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]He kissed her again, raising her hands above her head where he held both with one of his hands. He held them so tightly they felt like they were manacled to the wall. His other hand reached down and pulled up her dress, tearing it aside and reaching hungrily into it.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"No, Falamar," she yelled. Then when he wouldn't stop she bit his cheek.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]He let go of his dress and punched her full in the face, her head crunched against the wooden crate and seagulls along the dock yelled in complaint and took to flight. She started crying as he reached again for her dress.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"Did someone call me?" A man standing a the edge of the crates asked.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]The attacker, the man pretending to be Falamar, quickly let go of Chaeli and stepped away from the speaker. The speaker was a thin handsome man, lean and confident though he looked dangerous now, like a coiled snake. Though Chaeli felt unthreatened by him, her attacker felt differently and he immediately let go of Chaeli.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"Captain Falamar," he stammered.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"Issac?" Falamar answered, "I was sure I heard my name."[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Falamar, the real Falamar, kept advancing into the makeshift alley between the crates and Issac kept backing up. When Falamar reached Chaeli he asked her, "Are you okay?"[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]She nodded and tried to wipe the tears from her eyes. She could already feel her face bruising up from the punch.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"I'm sorry Falamar," Issac said, "sometimes I tell the gullie's I'm you. Just a bit of wishful dreaming I suppose."[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"That is not the crime I am concerned about." Falamar answered. Then Falamar struck, jumping forward he caught the larger man by the collar and slammed him back against the crates. Issac drew his knife but Falamar knocked it easily aside. With Issac trapped against the crate Falamar punched him, splintering Issac's cheekbone so severely it left his left eye rolling loosely in its socket and his cheek ran flush with purple blood.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"Go or I will give my sword to the lady and she will act out her desires on you, as you had intended for her."[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Issac scrambled away.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Chaeli, stunned into silence until this moment, fell suddenly into uncontrollable tears. Falamar tilted up her face, checking her bruise and as her sobs quieted her gave her a slight smile.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"Can I walk you home?"[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Chaeli only nodded in response. They walked in silence through the empty streets. Despite the trauma it was still a beautiful night and as they approached the squat flat Chaeli shared with her family she finally spoke.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"I thought... he said he was you."[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Falamar waited until they stood before her door before he answered.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"You deserve better than the Dunwich docks. Expect more from men, no matter their name."[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]She nodded, not really understanding.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"Will you be okay?" Falamar asked.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"Yes, my father is home. I will be okay, thanks to you."[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Falamar gave her another slight smile, said good night and headed back toward the docks. They were supposed to have set sail hours ago but Falamar was late as usual. He arrived to find the ship and the crew ready. Several men traded knowing glances as he came aboard.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"What was her name this time captain?" one called.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"I didn't ask." Falamar responded.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]His men laughed and cheered, they all assumed incorrectly but it boosted their spirits and Falamar saw little harm in it. The legend was certainly greater than the man, but when you regularly asked your men to face death sometimes it was easier if they believed a legend led them.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Amergin, Falamar's first mate, had already loaded the supplies and made sure the crew was on board and relatively sober. He had questions but had been serving Falamar since they were both boys, so he knew he would get the answers when Falamar was ready.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"Yes Amergin, we will be sailing out by moonlight. I have a contract from a Balseraph princess and it seems we need to make up some time. She pays well, and needs us to trap some animals for her."[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"Its an unusual task for you," Amergin commented.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"Easy gold and a damsel who needs help. It sounds exactly like me."[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Amergin smiled and ordered the crew to lift the anchor and set sail. Within seconds the ship was off to the Aegis Isles.
Keelyn giggles gleefully at the caged animals and construction of the upcoming Grand Menagerie. "This is wonderful," she squeals, "fetch me one of those big grey teethy beasts!"
Keelyn stares in amazement at the captured elephant. "I've heard of another pet, a chicken cat. Get one of those for me too!"

She was a delightful, if not demented, child and she twirled and danced between the animals we had assembled for her. Her courtier counted out the gold we had been promised and excused her behavior, though it was his disdain for her that bothered me far more than the young princess's enthusiasm.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]After checking each animal Keelyn approached me. She had a griffon feather in her hair and her dress, though once beautiful, was now patched and worn as if unable to keep up with the tiny tornado.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"These must be the most excellent animals from anywhere on Erebus!"[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]I smiled, "I am pleased that you think so, my hunters searched every corner of this island to find them for you. Where other princesses have rooms of toy animals, you will have the real things."[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]She grinned. This was my plan, to keep her focused on how wonderful it was. Her mind didn't dwell long on achievements and she was usually racing off to the next goal, and I had tired of searching this island for whatever she wanted next. But it was too late, her smile faded and her brow furrowed in thought. She was going to ask for more.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"It is a wonderful collection, but what about those that don't live on the island? What about those in the sea? The Lanun are talented fishermen, right?"[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"The best," I answered, at least this was the sort of hunting my men would prefer, "would you like us to gather some giant crabs, otolochs, or tortoises for you?"[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]She seemed to consider the suggestion, "No" she said, "do you know the giant wiggly beasts that are painted on the walls of the temple in Shaol?"[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"Yes, squids. They wouldn't survive long in your zoo I'm afraid. They had to stay in the water."[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Keelyn nodded, "Bring me some and I'll have Chuckles close in the harbor so they can't run away."[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Occasionally we caught squid in our nets, from those as long as a man's arm to those twice as long as a man. It wouldn't be much trouble to snare a few for her.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"Of course," I said loud enough for her snobbish courtier to hear, "we would be happy to capture a few squid for your collection, for the same price as the others."[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]The courtier sighed and looked as disappointed as Keelyn was excited.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"Load up the ships," I called to the men, "we do the rest of our hunting from beneath the white and purple, and atop a hull full of rum."[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]My men cheered and a few hours later we set out from the docks with a fair wind and high spirits.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE][NEWLINE]I dropped into darkness. I could hear the explosion of splintering wood and sense the movement of a giant around me. Something so great even the whales feared it. The central mast broke and plunged past me through the water. This was the only indication I had of direction, and I began swimming desperately toward the direction the mast came from.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]The seas were rough, but the Lanun like to say that just requires more drink to steady the ship. Though it was the perfect area for fishing our nets came up empty on every pull. We were preparing to move back towards the coast when the creatures attacked.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Giant tentacles reached up over the deck and crushed the ships as if they were made of paper. There was no coherent defense against this attack and the screaming of my men disappeared as the sea claimed me.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Just as I saw the shimmer of light through the inky darkness, as my lungs burned for air, I felt the tip of a tentacle close around my leg. I reached for my sword, but the sheath was empty. I had lost it in the water. A tug pulled me down, away from that golden halo of light and I fought for any way out of its grip.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]There was a single glint of metal in the darkness. It floated down from the remains of the ship and I reached to catch it. It was beyond my reach so I twisted against the tentacle, buying myself a precious few inches and I closed my hand around it. I immediately twisted back into the tentacle bringing the weapon to cut it from my leg. Only to discover that I only held a silver candlestick. In that moment my lungs exploded and I drank in the sea. All else disappeared.

Flauros looks up as Decius and his troops enter the palace. "Ah, commander, how go our plans?"[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Decius crosses his arms. "I've tried things your way. This Empyrean religion is only gaining followers. It is time to be more aggressive."[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"We have discussed why that is not among your options."[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"This Varn Gosam has called a meeting of tribal leaders. My spies tell me they are leaning toward uniting with him. Your foes will hold much more power in this region unless we act to stop them. I will take your army to the Malakim capital and burn it to the ground. That should keep the sand rats in their place."[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"You will act within the limits I have set for you. Or I will tear you to shreds."[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Decius raised blade. "Can you do so before I get in a single hit?" Flauros laughed, drawing his own blade, but Decius continued, "Because the Council's assassins have shown me a few things. Such as a rare desert plant, the extracts of which can cause a man pain like he's never known for as long as he lives. Perhaps you are willing to chance that over the course of your very long life you can find an antidote. Or that the effects will wear off after only a few hundred years. But why not chance that your power can be used beyond playing shepherd to a broken people, can rather shape the world stage to our benefit?"[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Flauros stood a moment, gazing at Decius. Then he sheathed his blade. "My sister would have killed you, and lived with the pain. Very well, take what you need. Raze every city with the Empyrean. If you bring calamity upon us, I will survive, and you will not, no matter the trump you hold. If your gamble succeeds, you will have a place among us forever."

The primitive encampment of the Hill Giants is razed, and the Giants themselves feeding the vultures. In one hut dwell a score of human slaves, their eyes lighting up at the sight of the destruction of their captors. One young man in tattered yellow clothes approaches Decius. "In the name of Lugus the Light, I thank you sir."[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"Who is this Lugus? Your feudal lord?"[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"Nay, good sir, he is the god of light, whose wisdom enlightens all the peoples of this desert."[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Decius yanks the mans chains, pulling him to his knees. "Not wise enough to keep you safe, nor alert you when you speak to a foe." [NEWLINE][NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Flauros is pleased to see that Decius has the mettle he suspected. Less so to hear of the Ecclesiastic. "I have not seen a priest of Lugus for over six hundred years, and now one appears on my borders? This is an ill sign."[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Decius raises an eyebrow. "Six hundred years? The Prelates spoke of devil-men living in the desert of Myrh. I hadn't expected they were being quite so literal."[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"I have no allegiance to Hell, simply similar tactics-extracting power from mortals. I trust this doesn't strain our working arrangement?"[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Decius shrugged. "I've little illusions about how you treat your subjects. What you do with their souls is even less my concern. I've passed your test. What is next?"[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"The Bannor were fools to discard such a useful tool as you. Efficient and heartless. But I need guile as well. Lugus is an old foe, and not one to release a grudge. His cult gaining ground here means trouble for us. I need you to strike down these Ecclesiastics, without drawing us into direct confrontation with the desert tribes."[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"I've seen your power. Give me command of a larger force of vampires and we can be ruling this entire desert."[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"I have shared our secret with you, Decius, but wish it to remain that. If we take ourselves into the battlefield, we will be hunted down by all the nations. Better to stay on the edges of the civilized world. Lugus has other enemies that may aid us, however, without asking questions. Let us encourage the Council of Esus among our lands, and train men who can strike without revealing their masters. Use them to eliminate the disciples of Lugus, and the power I wield may be yours."[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"Very well, we will do this your way, Flauros."

An obese, pale man, carried on a litter by a slaves watches Decius training his units for the assault on Dirage. Decius walks over after organizing a scout patrol. "I don't suppose you've come to enlist," he says. The man has the clear signs of Calabim aristocracy, but Decius takes a measure of satisfaction from refusing to acknowledge it.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"I am the governor of this city. Flauros decrees that I must cooperate with you, find out what you need to research for your task. It pleases him to give this authority to such as yourself, for reasons I couldn't grasp."[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Decius thought for a moment. "If I am successful, I will have the cusp of an empire. Feudalism would be useful for this, though..." He glanced up at the governor, realizing he wanted more than to build an empire for lazy fools like these. Deception. Poison. Tools like these could help him in a conflict with his benefactor Flauros or other foes to come. Religion was a useful tool for controlling a nation, but he decided it would be a poor idea to invite such foreign influence and invite the eye of meddling goods.

Decius has fled the Bannor, seeking refuge across the sea. In the desert of Myrh dwell the Malakim, a morally upright people. He has had his fill of moral presumption, however, and seeks shelter amongst a more ethically flexible culture.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]The Calabim are an ancient order whose aristocracy prey on the weak of their society. Weakness has long since been drilled out of Decius.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE][NEWLINE]It is a blighted neighborhood on the outskirts of Prespur over which Decius has exerted influence. Between the battered humans who have had their wills broken and those petty thugs just strong enough to prey on them, he has no competition for the petty fiefdom he sets up, so long as the aristocrats do not deign to enter.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Flauros, second born of all vampires, has seen this play out many times before. It is a replay of the Calabim social structure on a smaller scale, and he delights in letting the local lord know who is really on top.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Decius knows he is playing a dangerous game. When the bloodpets of the Vampiric lord come, his army is alert and dispatches them promptly. Flauros himself, however, is harder to handle. He personally slays Decius's army of exiles and criminals, leaving the bodies for the Moroi. Decius himself is far too interesting to do in, however.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"We have few immigrants here, and fewer still with your skills. Why do you come to our land, only to wallow in the filth of the livestock?"[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Decius folds his arms. "I kept every code and rule of my home, only to have them turn me out. I am through with rules and submission to authority. I will rise to the top, or die on my feet."[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Flauros smiled. "Whether you know it or not, you have come to the right place then. Our nation is a meritocracy in ways the Bannor would never hope to emulate. Those undeserving are consumed, while those who prove themselves are rewarded beyond their keen. I offer you a chance to start down this path. I will give you command of a small force. Eliminate the Hill Giants that have been preying on our countryside."[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Decius nodded. "Very well. But with the rabble you call soldiers, I don't give good odds of my survival."[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"Either way it will be entertaining."

Decius earned a place among the Calabim through grit and guile, and has forced them to take a more competitive place among the nations of Erebus. Just as a competition is heating up on the other side of the desert of Myrh. Word comes through the Undercouncil of dark plans reaching fulfillment, as the Sheaim complete their masterstroke and unleash the Infernals into the world. This is not as the Calabim would have preferred, but does present opportunities. Flauros offers Decius the opportunity to see how best he can exploit this brutal war. The remnants of the Malakim have taken arms in defense of their friends, so Decius sets out in a fleet of ships to flank them on the foothills of Tempus Mor.
Description: Follow Decius as he flees into the desert.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Requires: Successful completion of the Fall of Cuantine scenario.

Varn was a difficult man to find in the weeks after his revelations. Decius came upon him sending out a group of messengers, and he turned to Decius to explain, "We can no longer tarry with the tribes of this desert. I will call a council meeting. A desert custom I hope to incorporate into the Overcouncil. Those that adopted our faith will join with us, but I fear we will alienate those that did not. Either way, your task has not changed, just expanded. You need to spread this faith throughout the region. It must become the dominant creed here for our alliance to last. Beware the Calabim, for they will surely continue to oppose us."[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Varn turned to go, anxious to oversee some Vicar's training, or perhaps give guidance to a caravanner. Decius stopped him with a hand on his shoulder. "I am not sure I like this goal, Varn. My people were united by the Order of Junil, it is true, but I now see that their zeal was not without a grave price, a price I do not wish to extract in pursuit of your cause either."[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Varn smiled. "The tactics are up to you, Decius. We need not seek destruction of the Calabim, wicked as they may be, if our missionaries are able in their persuasion, and likewise you can try to avoid bringing harm to those of the desert that oppose us. But the desert is a harsh place, and I need a man of steel like you that I can depend on. For your tactical mind, and for a friend who will voice his concerns should our task overwhelm my judgment. With haste, perhaps a band of Ecclesiastics will be enough. If not, the Vicars will be able to drive out competing creeds in our allied towns. Force is an allowable last resort, I'm afraid."[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Decius nodded and let Varn leave.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"At least you got to speak to him today." Decius turned to see Talia, the beautiful woman who had first given him a role in the Malakim-and Varn Gosam's wife.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"My lady."[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"Always with his priests these days. His work is a noble mission, but I confess I was happier before Lugus's worship was so codified, and my wisdom was sought as well. By day he is in meeting after meeting, training missionaries and scribes and hearing disputes among his faithful, clarifying dogma. And by night... well I am ready for him, but he is so exhausted!"[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"I will speak to him of your concerns, then," Decius said, stepping back.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"Thank you, Decius. You are a good friend, and like the Varn I love in so many ways." She gave him a kiss on each cheek before leaving him to his duty; a custom in the desert, though not a common one in this day. Decius steeled himself to his task. He had known countless women widowed by war, women with complaints that dwarfed Talia's, but her loneliness was genuine. The Varn she had pledged to was not the one so consumed with his goals... but such is life.
