Description: Protect the citizens of Bourne the Gleaming until they complete the Mercurian Gate. Kill 100 Infernal units before any attack Bourne to win.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Special Rules: Player cannot go farther west than the starting location. The Infernal receive free units in their cities every turn.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Requires: Successful completion of the Momus scenario.

Rhoanna spoke to the unit commander in hushed tones. He wore the same golden armor as his men, but had passed through a few more winters, and his authority was obvious from the respect his men showed him. Falamar noticed that black tattoos snaked up from under his armor and wrapped around his neck and his left hand was covered with intricate tattoos, which was highly unusual for a commander of the Radiant Guard. He also looked pained, stressed beyond even the ravages of war.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Rhoanna walked back to where Falamar and the crew waited.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"He says Bourne is threatened from internal and external forces. He wants us to lead the troops in the field, to keep the Infernals from attacking Bourne while they fight the heretics inside the city."[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Falamar walked close enough that they could talk without anyone overhearing.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"Who is the commander? He looks afraid of more than death."[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Rhoanna glanced back at the commander who was in the process of splitting his men, some to return to the city and other to stay and await orders.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"His name is Mikel, he's the son of an Emry," she answered. "He grew up among the Sheaim before splitting and dedicating his life to the Empyrean."[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"That explains the tattoos. But that should make him less afraid of war."[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"The heretics have captured his wife and three-year-old daughter. They demanded he take his men and abandon the city and he has refused. There isn't much hope he will be able to save them."[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]She said this last part softly, but Mikel was behind her and had heard it. If the words affected him he didn't show it.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"I am the shield until the sword comes free," he intoned. "If you hold the line here I will scourge the heretics form Bourne and Basium will have a base to launch his war from. If the Infernals slip through your line then Bourne will fall and the devils will consume this land. I will give you some of the guard to stand with you. Will you battle Hyborem?"[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"Yes," Falamar answered without hesitation, "take care of Bourne and leave the devils to us."

Verchiel dropped to his knees and cried. He was an angel of Lugus, lord of the dawn and revelation, but he was unable to deliver his message. He knew where Mikel's wife and daughter were imprisoned, Verchiel was kneeling beside them in the ether. But Mikel was too full of fear and doubt to hear the angel's voice. The city's priests either didn't understand the message or were too busy praising the victory against the Infernals. Even now the heretics sat in the barrack's main hall planning to kill their two prisoners and dump the bodies into the sewers. They were only one floor above them and after weeks of being held within the barracks, the prisoners only had a few minutes left to live.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"Why are you crying?"[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Verchiel stopped in surprise. He looked up to see Meegan, Mikel's three year old daughter looking at him quizzically.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"Can you see me child?" Verchiel asked, equally puzzled.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"Of course. What is your name?" she asked.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Hallah, Meegan's mother, sat staring at the iron-bound door of the cell as she had for weeks. The room they were trapped in was an old storage room, and still had a pile of old tools and supplies in it. She had been through it a dozen times but there was nothing that could help her escape. She tried to stay strong while Meegan was awake, and save her tears for when her daughter was sleeping. She was so lost in her thoughts it took her a minute to realize Meegan was holding a conversation with an old broom.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"Chipmunk, who are you talking to?"[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Meegan smiled, "His name is Verchiel, he's an angel and he will help us get back to daddy."[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Hallah had no words. At three years old her daughter had gone crazy. Hallah wasn't sure if she should be jealous of her daughter's hope, or condemn her for it.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"We need something shiny," Meegan said, going again through the pile of supplies. She finally found an old copper plate that seemed to satisfy her and she cleaned it as well as possible with the hem of her dress.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Hallah heard the door to the basement open. This time instead of the single footsteps of someone bringing them food she heard a group coming down the stairs. Hallah pulled Meegan into her arms and when she squirmed Hallah told her to be quiet.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]There was a jingle of keys and then the door opened. Six men, all of the conspirators were here. Two had swords drawn, one a knife and another had a rope he looked about to put to use.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"Sorry deary," he said, "your husband's too stubborn for his own good."[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]At that Meegan tore free of her mothers grip and stood protectively in front of her. She held the polished copper plate above her head and the men stepped back a bit at the sudden move. Nothing happened.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Then Meegan asked the broom, "what do I say?"[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"Come on deary," the man carrying the rope said, "ain't no joy in killing a child. But it's either you go into the sewers or I go into the dungeon, and I ain't fool enough to consider that."[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"You cannot hide your actions," Meegan shouted in a voice half her own and half unworldly, "Lugus will reveal all. If you mean to escape, then flee now into the darkness; this area has been claimed by the rose of summer!"[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Hallah was more surprised than the men and they took a stunned step backwards. But realizing that no matter the threat they weren't about to be cowed by a three-year-old with an old plate, one of the swordsmen stepped towards Meegan.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]The copper plate exploded in light. It was as if Meegan held the sun itself above her head. The men covered their eyes in pain, light flooded the storage room, the hallway and up into the barracks itself. Breaking free of every window or crack in the barracks walls light came spilling out onto the dark streets of Bourne. The Radiant Guard knew immediately that the power of Lugus was manifest within the city and rushed toward the barracks.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]One of the kidnappers yelled for his men to stand firm. The light burnt through to his eyes even when they were closed and covered by his arm. He placed his sword in front of him and risked one peek at where he thought the little girl was standing. When he looked he saw a golden angel standing before him with a blazing sword.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"You will not harm these people," the angel said.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]The heretics fled up out of the barracks and into the street where they were met by the radiant guard and quickly arrested. Mikel was just starting to question one when his wife and daughter stepped out of the barracks. If there is any true hope or happiness left in Erebus, it existed there as Mikel swept them both up into his arms. It was hours before he let go of either of them.

The savant examined Mikel. Mikel was tied to a post that had been erected behind a small granary. The Infernals had several people tied up within the city and refused to kill anyone yet, and they wanted to make sure none of the prisoners could see each other, so each was alone. But they could hear each other in pain and agony. It was worse to imagine what was happening to the others than to actually see it. Especially with the horrifying demons that now walked the streets of Bourne. Except for being tied up Mikel had been left alone, but apparently it was his turn now.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]A few members of the Sect of Flies came into the yard. They were decrepit and foul. They were named for the thousands of flies that lived on and about them, but worse parasites lived and feasted in their flesh. Their skin crawled with the pressure of the creatures that burrowed within it and their stench was like sweat and rotten flesh, as if a corpse had gone for a long jog.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Mikel wasn't afraid. He had seen horrible things when he lived among the Sheaim and he had already accepted that he was to die here. He prayed to Lugus for the purification of his soul, for forgiveness for his own weakness in being unable to protect the city, and for the souls of his wife and daughter who had been taken from him weeks ago. He was not afraid until he saw who they dragged out into the yard.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]It was his wife Hallah. She was still alive, but beaten and bruised. They hadn't killed her, for a moment he was grateful for that, until he realized what they had saved her for.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]The Sect of Flies started by pulling off her clothes. She screamed and looked at Mikel in terror and shame as they debased themselves upon her. Their parasites fed on her as well, and they spread through any placed they touched. For hours they abused her in increasingly painful ways until finally her spirit was broken and she just lay quiet as they acted out their desires upon her. In time the burrowing parasites could be seen under her flesh and her body twitched and spasmed to the pain of being consumed from the inside out.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]By the time Hallah died Mikel had no prayers left in him. He had threatened, screamed, cried and finally begged for it to stop but the devils had ignored all of it. Mikel questioned everything in his life that lead him to this moment, was sorry for every decision. And that was before they brought out his daughter. By the time that torment was done the only thing left within Mikel was pain and hatred.

Description: The first summer in over 400 years finds the Svartalfar and the Ljosalfar returning to their ancient home to rekindle their civil war. You fight the battle to see what elven nation will survive in the Age of rebirth.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Special Rules: Each turn is represented by one of 8 day cycles: Dawn, Morning, Noon, Afternoon, etc. Different events trigger on different turns. Baron Duin's forces turn into werewolves every dusk and back to men at dawn. When Sucellus withdrew from Erebus his children were left to rule themselves. They decreed that they would be ruled by two queens, each for half of the year. One queen ruled the summer court and under her the elves nurtured beauty and art, and trained in the vigilant defense of their empire. The other queen ruled the winter court which was made up of the mischievous members of the fey kingdom, the tricksters, illusionists and those fond of laughter and nights spent dancing under the stars. It continued like this all through the Age of Magic, the elven empire grew and revered Sucellus.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]That lasted until the god of Winter entered creation and dropped Erebus into an unending winter. Faeryl, queen of the winter court, refused to abandon her throne for as long as winter remained. The elves prayed for help and Sucellus answered, coming personally into creation to battle the god of winter. But Sucellus was killed in that battle and his children were left alone and godless.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Faeryl ordered that the worship of a dead god was useless and that the empire should instead revere Esus, the god of night and deception. The shrines of Sucellus were torn down, the priests unwilling to abandon their old faith were rejected from the elven nation. But the summer court rallied against this. Under Arendel, queen of the summer court, they raised an army and attacked the members of the winter court dropping the elves into a bloody civil war.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]As the world continued to cool from the presence of Mulcarn and the death of Sucellus it became less and less habitable. In time only small isolated pockets remained where the bands of elves could survive. Between the civil war and the cold both sides neared extinction. Eventually the winter made travel and attacks impossible and both sides were forced to put aside their war.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Over 400 years later Mulcarn was killed and summer returned. The surviving generations of elves were able to travel again, and they have not forgotten the Umbrawood, their ancient homeland, or the war that has not been settled. Now they meet again within the Umbrawood and this war must be played out to see who will control the elves in this new age.

Faeryl was laid to rest with the honors due an elven queen. Though many argued against a funeral for an enemy leader, Arendel had demanded it. As controversial as it had been no one questioned it now and the massive funeral was properly somber and respectful.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Of the former Svartalfar, all those that had sworn allegiance to the summer court were invited to attend. For the first time in two ages the Svartalfar and Ljosalfar united in a common task, even if it was to mourn the death of the winter queen. They stood up and eulogized her and Svartalfar and Ljosalfar alike shed tears for Faeryl. Even Arendel stood and spoke lovingly of her sister, the fallen queen.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]That night the funeral procession passed through the streets of Evermore as starlight glistened off of the silver and mithril coffin. As was tradition her coffin was displayed within the Temple of Leaves for the night and then moved to the hidden tomb used to house elven royalty in the morning. By then thousands of gifts were brought to the temple and laid around the tomb.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Just before dawn horns summoned all the citizens of Evermore to the city's grand plaza. Once everyone was gathered Arendel came out onto the palace balcony and addressed them.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"We must not forget. We must not forget our legends, the days spent within this very wood as the children of Sucellus and Cernunnos. We must not forget that age we spent on our own as a single elven nation and the trials and fortune we shared. And we must not forget that we turned to war with each other."[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"Every memory we have is shared, every glory, every defeat. We are one people, and we were even as we killed each other."[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"Long ago, Sucellus anointed two queens to lead us so that the passions of one person could not lead our empire into ruin as happened with the empire of men. But this split led to civil war."[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"Through prayer and careful deliberation with the priests, sages and captains of both former empires we have decided to form a new high council. That there would be two elven queens and an elven king to lead us. That these leaders would rule year round within their own nations and that they would come together to decide matters for the empire."[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"I will be the queen of Evermore, of the temples and over the monuments and artifacts of our empire. I will tend to the orchards and provide for the musicians, artists and craftsmen. Brave Amelanchier will be anointed as king and assigned our army, given provision over our forts and made responsible for our defense. He will also take charge of our hunters and be responsible for the lands untended within our borders. Thessa will be anointed as queen and responsible for all manners of study, arcane or mundane, as well as diplomacy and trade with other lands. If military action is to occur outside of our empire then it will be under her leadership."[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"If you are a child of Sucellus then you are a member of our empire. A particular faith is not a requirement and the former Svartalfar are equal in every way to other citizens. The war is over and if we are to shed tears then we must do so together. If we are angry then we must be angry with ourselves. As mighty Sucellus was destroyed by winter and split apart until Nantosuelta gathered his pieces back together for his resurrection, so are the Ljosalfar. Now rejoined we are reborn, and I pray that will ever be so."[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]As dawn struck the plaza the Ljosalfar palace seemed to glow with an aura of gold and white. It was a new world for the Ljosalfar and they couldn't help but feel hopeful that it would be a kinder world than they had known for centuries.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE][NEWLINE]That night, after to coronation of Thessa and Amelanchier and seeing them off to their remote capitals Arendel retired to her personal chambers. After checking the magical wards that protected the rooms she removed her amulet and watched in the mirror as the illusion melted away. Her long blond hair shortened to wavy black. Her skin paled to cool alabaster. Her body shifted from the lean beautiful form of the elven queen to her own more sensual and curved body.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Far away, beneath the great red oak of Evermore, within the hidden tomb for elven royalty, behind powerful guards and locked within a silver and mithril box the real Arendel screamed.

The messenger of Esus was one of my favorite creations. He had two mouths and always spoke both the truth and lies. He was currently standing before the court simultaneously telling of the victory of the Svartalfar and of the Ljosalfar. Demonic barons planned both my triumph and a way to recover from this defeat depending on which story they believed. Of course as I am able to discern every lie; it is of no hindrance to me.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]The messenger addressed the masked figure in the throne, who sat in the deepest shadows of the long hall. Everyone assumed that was Esus, in fact my deception was so complete that even the decoy in the throne believed he was Esus when actually I was disguised as a simple lyrist in the hall. These past few centuries I had begun to wonder: what if everyone in the hall believed that they were Esus and I wasn't in fact the god of deception? But it was a thought I tried to chase out of my mind.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]I could see everything done in shadows, hear everything whispered. In a distant cell Ljosalfar prisoners planned for an escape, Rivanna herself considered overthrowing Faeryl, and all throughout the Umbrawood those few elves who remained loyal to Cernunnos hid.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Across the rest of Erebus greater lies are being told by priests, generals and kings. I closed my eyes and buried myself in the layers of manipulation, intrigue and egoism.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]But there was one cancerous sore on Erebus, one place devoid of the subtleties of my work. The Dead Lands, where walking corpses spoke their own simple truth and Tebryn Arbandi sought to end my game entirely. There is no opportunity in destruction, and as much as my wayward sister may object, I had no desire to see my kingdoms turned to ash.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]So I whispered into Faeryl's ear. I told her tales of desire, wealth and power and beneath a white moon the Svartalfar launched warships towards the Dead Lands.

Flauros had come to observe the progress Decius was making, and they consulted over dinner. Decius was eating the last stores of an elven city recently conquered, as it was getting harder to find decent food as Hyborem's corruption spread. Flauros merely sipped his imported wine. A fire crackled as they discussed the final battle plans, causing shadows to dance on the castle's walls.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]One of the shadows detached itself, however, and dove towards Decius, knives in each hand. One pierced the warrior's side, and he fell from his chair. Flauros watched calmly as Decius rolled aside and removed the knife. The wound wasn't bad, due to his light armor. The assassin lunged again, and Decius barely moved aside. He grabbed the man's arm and swung him into the wall, stunning him with a sickening crunch.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Flauros pushed himself back from the table and rose. "Very well done, my friend. With this invader as well as the entire Tempus Mor gambit. They say the best revenge is living well. I think you've earned the gift. Take this man's dying blood and I will show you the ritual we use to prolong our lives."[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Decius gazed at the cloaked man for a moment, then drew his blade and plunged it into the assassin's heart. Flauros smiled, but Decius cut him off with a "No."[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"You are refusing the gift?"[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"Yes, I am. If I were to live forever, I might end up like you. Weak and soft."[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]His patron replied by picking up the assassin and tearing his head off with his bare hands.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Decius continued, "You have physical strength, but you take it for granted. The cunning hunter has become the fat and lazy shepherd. Your immortality makes you content to sit back and let the world pass you by. I have walked alongside death and am not ready to abandon him now; I need this foe to keep my reflexes sharp and my plans focused.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Flauros studied Decius for a moment, then replied, "You no longer amuse me. I am returning to Prespur. You may do as you wish with those who will follow you, but do not return to my city on pain of death."[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Decius watched Flauros left, then smiled to himself. He turned to the dead assassin and said, "Now, that's a useful trick you have. Wonder if there are any more like you?"

Ethne stood again in the infirmary. People of many nations lay around her: Elven warriors, Sheaim prisoners of war, Malakim soldiers, religious pilgrims from around the world. Many, many more had passed through here since she had decided to deviate from the Elohim philosophy. A terror had been unleashed, and no doubt her name would be cursed by widows and orphans as Basium took his armies into all lands where the Ashen Veil reached. But her people had been saved, as had a core remnant of her allies. She had regrets, but life presented no paths free of regrets, and her Mercurian alliance was a choice she would again make.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"It will not be too much longer, Tuatha," she said to the monk who had been her shadow in the years of the war of Tempus Mor.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"Yes, my liege, there have been many fewer injured of our forces in the last months. And even fewer of the enemy killed or injured. Reports from Decius have been positive on his front as well, and the Ljosalfar refugees are eager to return."[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Ethne nodded. "This war may draw to an end soon, and we can tend to the people and land so harmed in it."[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"You have done enough." The voice came out of nowhere.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"This is a restricted area. If you have grievances-"[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"You cannot restrict us." This time the voice was from the other side of them. Ethne and Tuatha backed towards the hall. Other monks rose from tending the wounded and came to aid Ethne.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]It was to no avail. She backed into a cloaked man and before she had a chance to turn and see him his blade protruded from her chest. Tuatha grabbed the invader and threw him against the stone wall, then readied his mace and rushed towards him, but the assassin rolled past and into the hall, dashing away. When Ethne's protectors chased after, they found nothing.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Tuatha called for the castle arch-mage, but knew it would be to no use. He felt the theft of Ethne's spirit-resurrection would be no use.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"We must contact Decius. There may be other targets."

Decius directed his army to set up his camp on the foothills of Tempus Mor. The war had been long, and had hardened the Malakim recruits he led, but they stayed true to the Empyrean ideals, and had spared some remnant of his allies' civilizations. The eternal feud between Basium and the Infernals was sure to spread like fire to the rest of the world, as reports came in of Hellfire gates opening in distant lands through the actions of Sheaim agents.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]But Tempus Mor would have peace, and Varn's vision of an alliance of the good nations had borne fruit. Decius set a guard and headed into his tent to plot his next action. After some time he fell asleep on the ground beside his maps.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Late into the night he was awoken by a shout from his guard. As he rose he saw, from nowhere, an assassin's arm, dagger readied. Battle-hardened reflexes saved Decius's life, and he disarmed the assassin only to watch him begin to fade from view again. Whether this was some demon or wizard, Decius knew he had better find out who sent him. He grabbed a torch and swung it at the intruder to disrupt his spell. The assassin, a human man cloaked in grey, fell to the ground screaming and Decius's guards were able to subdue him.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Interrogation revealed an iron will in the assassin, but he was able to rule out the Svartalfar, Infernals, and Calabim as a source. As he mulled over how to get a motive out of his would-be killer, a messenger arrived. An Elohim monk with word that Ethne the White had succumbed to a similar strike, and magic was useless to revive her. If the Elohim ruler was to be restored, her assailant must be tracked down. And ignoring this threat would surely lead to future attempts, which might pierce his defenses. He had hoped to reinforce a city called Bourne the Gleaming, founded by Empyrean missionaries sent shortly after the first council in the desert of Myrh. But this mission south, into the wastes, took priority. With the secrets of the Mercurian Gate that Ethne had given them, they may be able to hold out against the Infernals summoned from the Hell-fire in lands of Os-Gabellas Sheaim ally, Tebryn.

Os-Gabella stalked alone, appraising the hellish landscape that greeted their progress here. This was once a forest, perhaps even an elven town, though little remained to suggest it. She stooped down and picked up a skull, then let it drop from her fingers. The Infernals' handiwork. There was a certain beauty to the emptiness that made her wistful. Her plan was a long-term one, and while she was well suited for patience, she longed for rest. "So far to go..." she muttered, dropping the skull.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"You've gone far enough." Os-Gabella whirled to see the speaker, a cloaked human man with a blade already poised to strike. She did not try to stop him. The strange hunter feinted and spun, impaling her heart in the blink of an eye."[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"Alas. I hadn't expected you would succeed." She grasped his head and began chanting. A moment later his body fell to the charred field, his head residing in a separate plane altogether.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE][NEWLINE]When Os-Gabella returned to Galveholm, the captain of her spies was waiting for her. "Interesting news, milady. Ethne the White of the Elohim has been slain."[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"Death is ubiquitous, or so I'm told."[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"Her archmages were unable to resurrect her. Apparently her assassin has a blade which could send her soul straight to the next world."[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Os-Gabella inhaled sharply. "Contact Decius. Offer him whatever he names if he retrieves this sword. Meanwhile, the chaos spreads. Already Infernal forces are coming to aid our Arch-mage ally Tebryn. They will surely defeat the Empyrean stronghold of Bourne the Gleaming, as is has been riddled from within by corruption. And all across Erebus, our war will spill. Come, end of all things. Bring me release."
Description: New alliances ignite a religious war in the mountains of Tempus Mor. [NEWLINE]Special Rules: Defeat at least 3 players of opposing alignment.[NEWLINE]Requires: Into the Desert.

Decius was waiting impatiently for the Emissary from the Ashen Veil to discuss strategy. Ritualists still made him uneasy. "Hello, Decius."[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Decius turned. There was a horseman greeting the Calabim leader that he did not recognize, until he removed his helm. "Rosier. You survived, then? I had thought the Order's hounds would have found you."[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]The fallen Oath-taker dismounted. "You'd be surprised what you can survive when you lose all limits. Or perhaps you wouldn't." Rosier laughed. Decius didn't. Rosier continued, "Once we defeat the Overcouncil, the Ashen Veil should have enough strength to challenge even the Bannor."[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"I thought the Ashen Veil cared more for the slow corruption method?"[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"Once we get the power we need, we can carry the torch to our enemies more openly. The Bannor are a dry husk of hypocrisy ready to be set ablaze. Can we count on your support when that battle comes?"[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"I think you get ahead of yourself. The Mercurians are a mortal threat to you unless we cripple them here and to the West, where they try to build a second gate with the help of the Radiant Guard. Should we prevail... I do not consider the Bannor worth mercy. I was betrayed. But I don't consider revenge my goal, Rosier, nor destruction. If your plans strengthen me, I will be there."[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Rosier nodded, and their talk turned to strategy.

Rumors have come in of a feared warrior in the forces of the Ashen Veil, a turncoat from the Bannor lands. He is known as Rosier the Fallen, and he has been torturing Malakim forces out of an apparent grudge with your ally Decius.

Ah, Decius. My old friend. What a pity to find you again opposing me.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Decius turns to see the brash young knight ride into his camp under a flag of truce. "Rosier. As I recall, I let you escape after your flaunting of the laws of the Order."[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"Really? That's not how I remember it. I was chased by the hound of the Order, Phanuel half-way across Erebus before I found refuge with the Sheaim. Refuge and more. They have power and aren't afraid to exploit it."[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"Hmph. The Bannor had me exiled as well-but I prefer the hound of the Order to the dog of Hell. I serve a more forgiving master now, but I am still just a servant. A soldier in the armies of good. Leave, before I test the bounds of that forgiveness by breaking the peace of your truce."

Ritualists painted symbols onto the armor the knight was to wear. It was midnight, and the blood they used came from warriors freshly sacrificed. Abnoba outlined the plans for the Sheaim forces, but he had other thoughts on his mind. "Decius is here, Abnoba. Leading Calabim forces."[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"Yes, this is true."[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"Why did you not tell me sooner? You know I want his blood. That and the blood of any fool of the Bannor."[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"We did not shelter you so you could defy our plans. But your hunger for revenge need not be frustrated if you look deeper. Decius has started down the same path you trod, the path that shall lead to him championing our ideals. He has seen the imperfection of the virtuous. He will find the emptiness of self and finally embrace the futility of existence. His life is forbidden you, but the path of destruction in Tempus Mor is wide. Now ride, Knight of the Veil."[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Rosier donned his helm and mounted. Taking up sword and shield he followed the path out.

An imp fell roughly from a portal into the dirt of the Calabim war camp. The Moroi jumped to their feet, but the creature waved them off. It crawled over to where Decius was sitting. The imp coughed black blood, and its wings hung limply. "Are you Decius?" it gasped. Decius nodded. "We were ambushed at the southern pass. A whole sect was destroyed. Our fort was burned and a senior Ritualist slain."[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"How many were there?"[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"One. One man on horseback. He let me escape so that I would tell you that he is here to take your head, Decius. And to tell you his name.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"Valin Phanuel."

The stalwart hero of the Order has been sent to help defeat the Infernals. "I hear the Malakim forces are led by one known as Decius. Is this so?"[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]The Elohim commander nods. "He came in Varn Gosam's stead, and has been a cunning and true ally to us."[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Valin turns away. "He is a fugitive from my homeland. This would be an opportunity to apprehend and try him. The menace posed by our enemies here make such a question moot, for the time being. Once this is resolved however, he has much to answer for."

Valin Phanuel rides into Decius' camp in the early morning. "Decius. I had not expected to see you here."[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Decius holds up his hand, motioning for Malakim guards to be ready. "Have you come to take me in, Valin?"[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Valin shakes his head. "No. You were, of course, tried in absentia and found guilty of desertion and heresy. I would be bound to take you captive to hear your confession and offer your sentence. But I have orders that take priority. The Bannor have sent a contingent to aid our friends the Elohim and Malakim against the great evil that has come to the world through Tempus Mor. I understand you are a commander of the Malakim faction here, so it will be my duty to aid you."[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"And after we are victorious?"[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"I will be duty bound to bring you back to the Bannor Empire... after I issue my report to the High Priest in person."[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"Elmin is here?"[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Valin almost smiled. "No. It will require a trip to Torrolerial. Should you be here when I return, however, we will conclude this business and your punishment will be meted."

The succubus that Os-Gabella kept as her chief of spies emerged from the mirror in her throne-room. "My deathless queen," the creature said bowing, half in flattery and half mockery. "Our ally Decius has brought his own enemies to this fight. From the Bannor lands come the Order's hunter, Valin Phanuel, hunting demons and heretics."

Decius attended the meeting of the Undercouncil in person. The current Calabim emissary, a corpulent vampire lord, glared at him from his seat when Decius entered. It mattered little to Decius-most of the vampiric aristocrats were angry with him for upsetting their hierarchy. He had the Brujahs on his side, though, for if he had his way they would have ample opportunity to prove their worth.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Decius skipped the formalities of the meeting, waiting only for the Svartalfar Speaker's invocation of Esus over the meeting before speaking.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"Our spies tell me that Varn Gosam traveled west with much of his army long before our assault on the Empyrean shrine. Specifically, to aid the Elohim against your armies and those of Hyborem. If the Malakim reinforce the Elohim to the east, they may hold out against your pet, and perhaps even save the Ljosalfar."[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"Faeryl Viconia will subdue our renegade cousins in the Umbrawood. Their fate is none of your concern."[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"And we care little of the ultimate fate of the Elohim. They have already brought in the Mercurians to aid them-this battle will inevitably engulf the world, bringing ruin. Your involvement is now irrelevant."[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Decius shook his head. "Bravado. Should the Calabim stay out of the Tempus Mor region and consolidate our position, it is quite likely that your Infernal allies will be stopped before they can establish themselves-and then the Ashen Veil will be destroyed, along with all the plots of the Sheaim. Varn Gosam may be willing to stop with that, but if the Order becomes involved-and they will, believe me-they will then turn on the Svartalfar, burning your forests to the ground if they must. No, clearly you have bitten off more than you can chew."[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]The Svartalfar Councilor smiled at Decius with murderous intent, but the Sheaim emissary replied, "Your words have merit. What do you want from us? Surely the spoils of this conflict will be enough to satisfy the needs of the Calabim? The blood of men and elves... this is what you crave, is it not?"[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"That would be enough to satisfy Flauros and Alexis. I want more. I want an empire. Everything from the taiga bordering the Umbra down the coast of the great Ocean to the Deruptus mountains, and west to the foothills of Tempus Mor."[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"Hmph. Is that all? The Svartalfar have no cares for the human lands."[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"Very well, Decius, we can come to an agreement. Your assistance here, and you shall be granted all the lands to the east-provided our Ritualists are granted access to the cities of the Calabim."[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Decius nodded, then turned to go. Should this battle result in victory, his empire would rival that of even the Bannor.

He found her in the infirmary. There were many among them who were skilled in healing arts; the Elohim temples and medical colleges were the most advanced in the world. So Ethne was not tending to the wounded directly, but rather to those so caught up in their work that they neglected themselves. She brought food to healers who were caring for the diseased, blankets for monks who had passed out exhausted among the burned or catatonic, and wiped away tears from priestesses caring for the maimed.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]As his shadow fell over her, Ethne turned and rose to face Einion. "Did you think you could deceive me?" he asked her.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Ethne bowed her head. "Deception is not a skill I posses, dear Logos. I merely neglected to consult about this course of action. Please do not take it as a sign of disrespect."[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Einion tapped his staff sharply on the ground, making an echo through the stone hall. "You are too coy child. I had to find out from Valoel, after he had already begun construction. Surely some madness has gripped you!"[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"Have you another plan? If so, I have not heard it. Os-Gabella has refused our ambassadors, and the Infernal reception was far worse. The Winter Queen has promised to bring peace to the forests, even as the people of Evermore are sold as slaves."[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"The lands that we have lost are unimportant. We can have the peace to continue our mission of preservation if we realize what is important. In these times of war, it is all the more important that we seek to save the knowledge that has been gained since the dawn of the Age. We have no need of these barbaric 'heavenly' warriors! As it was written in the times of our ancestors, 'Let virtue be your spear and faith your shield.'"[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Ethne turned her gaze around the room filled with burned pilgrims and their maimed defenders. "Which of these lacked virtue, then, and which lacked faith?"[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Einion was silent a moment, but not long enough for Ethne to think she swayed him. "A great many more will be so afflicted, and due to your actions our hands will be awash in the blood of the next victims. What you do here you do without my blessing. Oh great Sirona, why have I lived so long to see us come to this?"[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Ethne bowed her head respectfully as Einion retreated, then said softly, "If you live any longer, honored friend, it will be due to the warriors of heaven you so deplore."[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]The gate was built. It was everything Einion feared and everything Ethne prayed.

Decius watched the armies of the allied Malakim tribes array into a rough formation, each man with his arms and near his kin. There was much squabbling and joking; far from the ordered troops he had commanded on Bannor crusade. "They are not prepared for what we face, Vaughn."[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"We haven't embarked on a religious war before. We have no hardened crusaders among us. I count this a point in favor of the Empyrean, do you not?"[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"I do not count naïveté as a virtue when I march to war. Fanaticism is a vice I do not wish to import, but martial discipline will be critical if any of these men are to return."[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]The Vicar frowned. "It would be good if we could stay longer in this desert, where we have the advantage. But if our council is to sustain us in our hard times, we must stand with the Elohim in their dark hour."[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"Indeed. I would prefer to train them more, but what Varn Gosam tells me is cause for immediate mobilization. There is a dark and secretive people known as the Sheaim, and their schemes have reached fruition with an Infernal Pact. Agaress archangel Hyborem has entered our world. He has struck against the Ljosalfar, allowing our old enemies the Svartalfar an advantage in their war. The Elohim have brought in another ally, a force for good but not for peace-the renegade Basium and his warriors. Weakness in this war will bring destruction to the forces of good."

Abnoba oversaw the chanting of the ritualists. Not a word was misspoke. They had had the importance of this ritual made extremely clear. He turned to his queen, seated in her throne gazing impassively at the magic circle in the dim candle light.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"I cannot say that this will grant you what you seek, milady."[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"No, likely it will not. Hyborem's powers are great indeed, but even he lacks the power to rescind a blessing given by the twenty-one in concert. It seems I am destined to see the end of this world."[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"If anything would bring the apocalypse upon our world, it would be this ritual. Agares's followers will be bound to this world..." She trailed off as a sudden shaking almost knocked her to her feet. "Milady! Are we besieged?"[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"Abnoba... foolish child, what did you expect the rearrangement of the universe to feel like? Although doubtless the Bannor camp at our borders would take this as provocation and besiege us, and it would be to our advantage to let them face the Infernals and rip this land asunder... our spies tell us that they shall soon have to return home and face a worse surprise in the halls of Torrolerial. So we must find some other target for our new patron Hyborem."[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]The Ashen Veil priestess smiled. "The north."[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Os-Gabella beckoned. From the shadows came a Succubus. "If Hyborem has done his part from Hell, his forces should be emerging near Tempus Mor. The civil war of the Elven states should distract them enough for Hyborem to gain ground." The Succubus nodded and left the hall.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"And we?"[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Os-Gabella smiled. "As we have ever done. Bring discord and strife until this world is unfit for the great experiment it was built for."

A dusky lady in purple robes walked through the sandstorm outside the Calabim Palace. She was followed by a sand lion and a Malakim soldier holding a white banner of parlay. She was admitted to the forbidding antechamber of the palace by mocking guards, who brought her request for a meeting with their commander to Decius.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Decius allowed the meeting, and she was shown into his throne room. Her bodyguards and the bloodpets guarding the entrance were the only other people there. Decius said, "You are lucky that I am leading this force, lady. My patrons would not have so honored an enemy they had the advantage of. So you may speak, but I have a limit to my patience as well."[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]The lady nodded. "I am Talia Gosam, druid, and I come on behalf of the Overcouncil."[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Decius raised an eyebrow. "I had thought that your council had learned the futility of its existence in the desert of Myrh. Or were you absent during the sacking of Golden Leane?"[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"We all stand as long as one stands, and I trust you are not so foolish as to count this conflict won already. We are prepared to discuss terms with the Calabim separate from your allies."[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"Terms?"[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Talia said, "Our guide and god Lugus despises you and your wicked kin, but surely even you can see the threat posed by the Sheaim and the Infernals to the entire world! Your support for them is preventing our stopping this threat."[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"What about the Svartalfar?"[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"We would happily leave them out of this, or negotiate with them while we focus on the Infernals, but the past has proven that deals struck with Faeryl Viconia are unreliable. We can only hope that you have some measure of wisdom and honor despite your cruelty."[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"Cruelty? You don't know me, Talia. I am not the monster you might expect, although you will find such among my ranks, and my patrons. But I have as little use for cruelty as I do for honor. Your terms won't give me what I've already been promised, and I need not submit to righteous guardians in the process. Surely a druid understands the need to control one's own life, whatever the consequences?"[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"Speak not to me of my calling! You are allied with those who destroy the natural order wherever they step and would set the world aflame. There is redemption for you, Decius, if you will take it, but the Sheaim must be stopped. For the sake of all life! Think of this. Repent, and the Overcouncil will ensure your survival. That is all." Talia turned and left, returning unharmed to the Malakim forces.

Ethne traveled to Golden Leane to attend the meeting of the Overcouncil. Usually an envoy went in her place, but after recent gains in their mutual struggle she decided to go in person, especially to address the plight of Sheaim and Svartalfar prisoners of war. The Malakim were a good people, but their new commander Decius struck her as overly pragmatic. He deferred a great deal to Varn Gosam, however, and the Empyrean patriarch was a merciful elven man.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Chalid was at the council meeting, Varn Gosam's closest disciple, and another non-member: Varn's wife. Ethne greeted her before they formally began. "It is good to see you well, Talia. I think of you often when I hear of the destruction left in the wake of our enemies. There will be much work to do to return our land to order when we win here; perhaps you could aid our efforts in the savannah region Flauros has claimed."[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"Hmm? Oh, yes. These things trouble us all, of course. In fact, I will get a chance to see this area first hand as an envoy to the Calabim. They are unnatural monsters, but perhaps they can see that aiding this Hell on Erebus is not in their interest."[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"I'm sure you will be missed here as you travel."[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"We all have our roles to fill, Ethne. Our desires cannot interfere with our goals."[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"I simply meant..." Ethne's voice trailed off as Talia took a seat between Varn and Decius.

Decius returned to Golden Leane for the latest Overcouncil meeting. He was well used to his life, leading an army from the front lines, but he would enjoy sleeping in a bed, and the warmth of the desert. This winter seemed to be particularly harsh.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]On the road he was surprised to see a small company of the palace guard at an oasis. Then he noticed a woman meditating in the underbrush. He sent his personal guard ahead, and approached her.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"I thought that you had a garden at the palace for this," he said once she noticed him.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Talia smiled and rose. "Sometimes I need something a bit more wild. Varn was kind enough to assign his palace guard to keep watch for intruders, but it isn't needed. The wilds will guard me. Protection isn't what I need from my husband."[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]The two turned and began walking back towards the capital, the guardsmen following respectfully behind. "I have not met a druidess, before, milady, but I am surprised that you are drawn to the desert."[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Talia smiled and accepted the change of subject. "The dunes and barren rocks hold no joy for me, but here and there, in oases such as this, one find plants and animals of unequaled tenacity and cunning. This is nature as beautiful as any verdant elven forest, and this is the nature that I fell in love with when I first came to this desert. These are the same qualities that I saw in Varn, and you as well, Decius."[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"Tenacity? I have fled from my home rather than face false charges and defend my name honorably."[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"Honorable rabbits do not long survive hawks. Rabbits too frightful of them, though, would starve in their burrows. You pursue what you see as right, despite the trials you face."[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"Very well, I accept your compliment. Will you sit in on the Council meeting?"[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Talia nodded.

A Svartalfar spy was waiting in Os-Gabella's chambers when she retired for the night. "This game of Faeryl's may intimidate some, but it merely annoys me to have to kill so many of her spies," Os-Gabella said.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"I come with a message, dear friend of the Svartalfar. An opportunity. A tale of conversation overheard in the palace of a another friend. The wife of Varn Gosam, a woman of greatly divergent temperament, requests the Calabim withdrawal from our alliance. Decius declines the offer, overly politely. There is more here than diplomacy. A risk that Decius may be swayed, but as far as he has come, he has scant recourse to go back. If she were to have a moment of weakness though, it would stab at the heart of the Overcouncil."[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Os-Gabella smiled. "Perhaps if we alienate Decius... make him lonely, to long for a companion, he would seek out this woman in the future. Make sure he knows his fortune depends on his allegiance to us, however."

The Calabim hunters returned with unexpected prey from their patrol into the savannah at the edge of the desert of Myrh. Decius went out to meet them when they returned, to hear the reports from the Calabim's eastern front. He found the patrol stripping a woman. There was a sand lion corpse next to her that they had brought back as a trophy. Decius started to turn away; obviously there was nothing urgent to report. But he caught a glimpse of the woman's face.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"Stop." The vampire hunter who held the woman didn't notice the command, though his peers stood aside. Decius shoved him roughly aside. "I said stop."[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]The hunter snarled. His hand twitched by the handle of his axe, but his discipline held. He stepped back and said, "This is my spoils, commander. We found this wildling at an oasis, alone but for this beast here, which I killed. Let me take her."[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"This is no ordinary witch-woman; she is a Malakim noble. You will be rewarded for her bounty price. Was there anything else to report?"[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"No commander. The settlements we had heard of have been abandoned."[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Decius had Talia bound and taken to his tent. Shortly he returned there himself. He freed her bonds, but made a show of pointing out the silhouettes of his armed guards outside his tent.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"Surprising to see you again," he said. "Were you on another diplomatic quest?"[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"No. I was meditating. The cries of the natural order were agonizing, and I was distracted and subdued by your hunter. Thank you for your intervention."[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"It seemed a wasteful use of someone of your caliber."[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"So what use do you have in mind?"[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Decius studied her for a moment. "I haven't decided. Were I to follow the ways of my adopted people, I would take what pleasures your body offers and feast on your soul. Oddly, perhaps, this holds no appeal for me, and has the downside of wasting the resource of your mind. If I would take the example of the Bannor, I would try to discern the strength of your character and fidelity of your faith, then damn or free you based on that. While good for keeping discipline, I don't see my gain in that, either."[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"You have lived among the Bannor?" Talia said. "I have heard they are a people of unequaled zeal."[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"Yes. And blind devotion, unending war, and arrogance dressed up as virtue."[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Talia crossed her arms and gazed at the ground. "I fear my Varn leads us down this path as well. He brings the Malakim into conflicts that were not ours and ignores the wisdom others bring to meetings now devoted to Lugus. He has lost balance."[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"I would not be so ungrateful for advisors such as you. My allies have seen fit to give me Ritualists and mages to consult, magi who think little of my interests or that of my empire. I know you care little for my survival, but at least you would be honest about it."[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"I would never aid you while you side with the Infernal."[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"They do seem to be making a mess of these lands I would claim, but I cannot oppose them now. And your little Overcouncil is too weak to win at this point. Perhaps I can peacefully keep them from my empire, or gather allies to strike them in secret at a time of my choosing."[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"Do you think that my husband will let you detain me for your own use?"[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Decius shrugged. "It doesn't seem he was keeping a very close eye on you. Here is my decision, then. When Varn Gosam requests your return, you may leave unharmed. If you wish to give me your voice, or any other aid, I will welcome it."[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"You are kinder than I would have thought." Grudging respect was all Decius gained from Talia at first, but over the coming weeks she opened up to him, as he kept news of her capture a secret from ally and foe alike. She came to admire his strength and cunning, and bask in his attention. Finally, thoughts of her home and cause slipped entirely from her, and she embraced her captor.

The war was going well for the Overcouncil. Chalid took time from the front lines to bring news to Ethne.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"Varn Gosam is stepping down as Speaker of the Overcouncil, and has asked me to take his place. He is going to be leaving Golden Leane on a pilgrimage with his wife."[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"He is abandoning the war effort? He has been a great boon to the morale of the Empyrean soldiers in the field."[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"He says he has found competent people to take his place, in the council halls and on the throne. There is... more to it, however. A great sadness has crept into him. He can no longer focus on work that once consumed him. It is painful to see my good friend so troubled. In an unguarded moment, he spoke of a sudden betrayal by two he had trusted, for which he somehow blames himself. I would tend to him more closely, but as you say, the war is still at hand, and I have new duties to fulfill."[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Ethne placed a hand on his shoulder. "Thank you, Chalid. I wish you well, and I shall pray for Varn to be soothed and guarded by an angel of mercy. Agares the beguiler has plans beyond what we see play out on the field, and it would ill serve us to see our friend beset by grief."

The messenger found the commander in his camp. Decius was expecting news from Varn, and bid the traveler enter his tent.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"Hello, my friend," said the beautiful woman who entered.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"Talia. This is a pleasant surprise. So Varn trusts your safety in this rough country even in a war time?"[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"Perhaps he trusts me too much. Or perhaps he is simply not mindful of me. I no longer care. The message I've left with your lieutenant-something about Paladin training. It was just an excuse that I could see you."[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"Milady-Talia... Varn has been consumed with his service to Lugus, but..."[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"And saving the world is important, I know. I am a wretched vile woman for wanting a bit of time from our great savior!"[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"I did not say that. Your needs are understandable. But in a time of war, feelings are irrelevant to duty."[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"How will a few hours' time lose a war? Varn is not a soldier on the front lines. He is a man with his wife nearby. Why do we need to sacrifice our feelings when we are so close to each other? We could both be happy and attend our duties. And if Varn cannot see that... we could be happy." Talia put her arm on his shoulder.

Talia walked unescorted from the Calabim borders through the savannah. It was early morning, and she headed towards the rising sun, towards home. Decius had just released her from a captivity that she had forgotten wasn't voluntary. He had fascinated her, and she had betrayed her husband Varn Gosam to her baser instincts. But she learned much of the man whose armies opposed hers, and she comforted herself with the thought that this information might aid her people in stopping the Calabim.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"Do you know how the Sea of Sorrow was named?" The voice came from the shadows of a rock formation as she passed by.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"Who's there? I have been granted passage as a prisoner exchange by Decius of the Calabim."[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]An old crone in dusty purple robes emerged from the shadows. "There once was a great king who ruled over this land. Lord of all he would survey. His palace stood on a cliff overlooking the sea on the western edge." She paused.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Talia gave her no further prompting. "I have no time for your story. I am too long delayed from my home already." She turned away and hurried on, but found the woman ahead of her.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"It is his sorrow from which this sea draws its name. A great king who had everything he asked for given. And he climbed the tower stairs to throw himself to his death in the crashing sea beneath."[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"What concern is this of mine? Kings come and go; all creatures suffer. I must return to my people, who struggle with a threat to every living thing under the sun!" The dust around her feet rose swirling around her, cutting off the old woman, and again Talia turned towards home.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]This time she saw the woman step from thin air in front of her. "What caused a sorrow so great to make him disdain his own life? Do you not know the story?" The Crone looked into Talia's eyes, who this time held her gaze. "That which he most treasured was shown to be false. A promise shown a lie. A wife shown untrue."[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"Spirit be gone! Do not... do not judge me."[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"The king's greatest desire was for his trusted queen to stand loyally by his side and help him to rule justly. He was too kind to send her away, too wise to trust her again, too idealistic to live with his dream out of reach. His death was the only solution within his grasp."[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"It would be better had he never learned of this," Talia said softly.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"He will learn of it," the Crone said.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"He should... he can take another."[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"He is too true to do that. The king could not be happy... not while the queen who betrayed him still lived."[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]The old woman turned away, releasing Talia from her gaze. Talia shook her head, then turned away, running towards home.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]The crone's ancient façade faded away. She removed a small mirror from her robes, and sprinkled a powder over it, revealing a dreary castle in a hellish landscape. "The seeds are planted, Lethe. Follow this one. Take her guilt and pain as supplication, and lead her to your embrace."[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Then after one final look to the fleeing Talia, Os-Gabella spoke a arcane command and returned to her palace.

The Malakim soldiers fell silent when they saw who came into their war camp. Heads were bowed before Varn Gosam, the elf who had united them and shown them the light of their purpose. Varn Gosam smiled, speaking briefly with a few men before making his way to Decius's tent.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Decius looked up when Varn entered. He paused a moment, then said, "Varn, welcome. It is good to see you here. You should be safe, the tide of battle favors us, and seeing you will lift morale."[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"Yes, that is so. I will be sure to speak to them before leaving. But I came because I had to see you in person. I have a task to charge you with," Varn said.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"Much depends on the task I face here, my friend. I should not leave it until complete."[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"You have served well, in your official capacity, and I must ask for more of you. I am stepping down, for a while, at least. I have taken too much upon myself. Our goals are great, and require great effort. But they are so great they are beyond any one man, and as we have set the wheels in motion I must take some time for my own life."[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"Then my role?"[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"Take the lead of the Malakim. You have made an excellent general, and the men of the desert honor you for your skills and devotion. For a while, I ask that you guide the civil affairs of our people as well. Have a mage attend you, and use divination to communicate with the council in Golden Leane. This will take some of your time from here, but you should have competent commanders you can promote to lead from the front."[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Decius nodded. "I will do this for you. So you will devote yourself to Lugus's work on the Overcouncil?"[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"No. Chalid has been attending the council meetings with me, and he shall take over as Speaker in my stead. Vaughn will return to Dies Dei and take the mantle of Patriarch."[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"Very well. May I ask what prompted this retirement?"[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Varn shook as head and turned to leave, then paused with his back to Decius. "We preach openness, I so suppose it should not go unsaid. Your recent actions when my Talia was visiting here have demonstrated how much I was failing my other obligations. It was my hubris to think that I could cause no harm while pursuing the good with such dedication. The same mistake made by the priesthood that so failed you, I suppose. The marital bond that sustained me I neglected; now I must see if it can be made strong anew. Take care, Decius, and take care of my people."

Welcome to Fall from Heaven II.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Since this is your first time playing it may be worth taking a few minutes to describe some of the basics. First the tech tree, there are a lot of tech options. I would recommend teching toward Archery for your first game. Barbarians are more common and powerful in Fall from Heaven and players often underestimate the amount of early defense that is required to protect your cities.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]After getting to Archery you will need to build some Archery Ranges in your cities before you can build Archers. This is a common mechanic in Fall from Heaven (units require buildings) that forces specialization in your cities and an a deeper investment in the troops you wish to create. Once you have the Archery Ranges you will be able to build Archers. It may be more effective to build an Archery Range in one city and use that city to produce Archers to protect all your cities.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]After Archery there are a wide variety of tech options to consider. For your first game I would suggest you stay away from the magical techs early on, like Knowledge of the Ether and anything behind it.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Here are a few special mechanics you may have early questions on:[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Weapon System- Copper, Iron and Mithril give strength bonuses to melee units (and a few others). This is a considerable advantage and even warriors get +1 strength if you manage to get access to Copper.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Lairs- It is a dangerous world, and it has a mix of monsters lairs spread across it. These lairs will produce new barbarian units until they are destroyed. You can destroy them by moving a unit onto them and selecting the action button to explore the lair with that unit. Be careful, although exploring a lair could result in finding treasure or other rewards it can also release new enemies or powerful boss monsters.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Heroes- There are barbarian heroes, civilization heroes and religious heroes. Which ones you have access to depends on what techs you have, what civilizations you are playing as and which religion you have. They are all very powerful but once they are dead they are dead forever, so be careful in their lose and when you see them nearing in your enemies hands. One of the barbarians heroes, Orthus, is a powerful orc warlord that may spawn near you. If so make sure to have your defenders ready as he has killed many civilizations.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Have fun and try things, most get crushed in their first few games. The strategy's that have worked ever since Civ1 won't work here. But hopefully you will enjoy exploring the world of Erebus.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Keep in mind that there is a lot to try in Fall from Heaven. There are scenarios you can play from the main menu -> single player -> play a scenario -> "Fall from Heaven II scenarios". There is a mini-game called Somnium you can challenge other human and AI players too (the icon in the upper left that looks like a pawn opens the Somnium menu). The civilopedia has a lot of good information in it, be sure to check out the concepts section or more details on a lot of the Fall from Heaven special mechanics.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]After you are done playing please come to the forums link on www.civfanatics.com/ffh to provide feedback, ask questions and find player to play multi-player with.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Thank you for playing,[NEWLINE]the Fall from Heaven Team
